Extraordinary teams building inspiring projects:

Since 1898, we have helped customers complete more than 25,000 projects in 160 countries on all seven continents that have created jobs, grown economies, improved the resiliency of the world's infrastructure, increased access to energy, resources, and vital services, and made the world a safer, cleaner place.

Differentiated by the quality of our people and our relentless drive to deliver the most successful outcomes, we align our capabilities to our customers' objectives to create a lasting positive impact. We serve the Infrastructure; Nuclear, Security & Environmental; Energy; Mining & Metals, and the Manufacturing and Technology markets. Our services span from initial planning and investment, through start-up and operations.

Core to Bechtel is our Vision, Values and Commitments . They are what we believe, what customers can expect, and how we deliver. Learn more about our extraordinary teams building inspiring projects in our Impact Report .

Project Overview:

Bechtel is building a semiconductor manufacturing plant in New Albany, Ohio. We are partnering with the North America Building Trades Unions and suppliers to create several thousand new jobs and work with local education organizations to implement new training programs that will support the future talent pipeline. Bechtel Manufacturing & Technology, Inc. offers engineering, procurement, and construction services for customers in the semiconductor manufacturing, electric vehicle, and data center markets. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, the M&T global business unit also includes colleagues working in Arizona, Ohio, Texas, India, and additional project locations around the world.
M&T strives to exceed our customer objectives through utilizing our agility, innovative technologies, and world class talent. M&T will solve the industries toughest challenges, building both our company and the world for the future.

Job Summary:

The Lead Instrumentation & Controls (I&C) Commissioning and Startup (CSU) Engineer is responsible for the technical leadership, planning, coordination, and execution of commissioning, startup, testing, troubleshooting, and turnover activities for instrumentation, controls, automation, and process monitoring systems within a large semiconductor manufacturing facility.
This position supports the successful transition of systems from construction completion through operational readiness and handover to the client. The Lead I&C CSU Engineer ensures that all instrumentation, control systems, PLCs, SCADA/BMS systems, process control networks, field devices, and associated interfaces are installed, tested, commissioned, and operated in accordance with project requirements, design specifications, industry standards, and safety expectations.
The role serves as a key interface between Engineering, Construction, Quality, Vendors, Operations, and Client stakeholders throughout the startup and commissioning lifecycle.
• Collaborate: Actively seeks out others' opinions and input and is open-minded to their views. Challenges others appropriately and is also open to being challenged on their own views.
• Communicate: Is effective at adapting their communication style appropriately to their audience, providing context and using the right tone and level of information.
• Customer Focus: Prioritizes the customer needs and puts these at the forefront of all interactions. Ensures that others within their team maintain this same approach.
• Deliver: Demonstrates making well thought out, timely decisions and prioritization that leads to successful outcomes. Includes the right people at the right time.
• Problem Solve: Accurately assesses a situation to find the best solution or way of working to resolve the issues. It is focused on creating a long term fix rather than a short-term solution.
• Role Model: Contributes to the Bechtel culture by inspiring and motivating others through their positive approach and attitude. Comes to work determined to do a good job, for themselves and for their team.
• Adaptability: Deep understanding of interconnected technology systems and how to troubleshoot them while they are actively running.
• Compliance: Ensure all procedures and equipment setups meet regulatory, OSHA, and environmental safety standards.
• Troubleshooting & Diagnostics: Resolve complex failures involving computer hardware, network routers, switches, and software interfacing directly with control equipment. #LI-AA1

Major Responsibilities:

Commissioning Leadership
• Lead and supervise I&C commissioning engineers and commissioning specialists.
• Provide technical guidance, mentorship, and oversight of commissioning personnel.
• Develop commissioning strategies that support project turnover and startup milestones.
• Foster a strong safety culture and ensure all commissioning activities are executed safely and efficiently.
• Coordinate activities between construction, systems completion, startup, operations, and vendor representatives.
Planning and Preparation
• Develop commissioning plans, procedures, test packs, turnover packages, and acceptance criteria.
• Participate in commissioning scope development, constructability reviews, HAZOPs, operational readiness reviews, and startup planning activities.
• Review P&IDs, control narratives, logic diagrams, instrument datasheets, loop drawings, network architecture diagrams, and vendor documentation.
• Support development of commissioning schedules and turnover strategies.
• Assist in identifying system boundaries and turnover packages.
System Verification
• Verify installation and configuration of field instrumentation, analyzers, control valves, PLC systems, distributed control systems, building management systems, and process monitoring equipment.
• Confirm instrument calibration, communication protocols, network connectivity, and equipment readiness.
• Verify safety interlocks, permissives, alarms, and shutdown functions.
• Ensure construction completion and documentation requirements are met prior to startup activities.
Commissioning Execution
• Lead field walkdowns and punch list management activities.
• Execute instrument loop checks, functional testing, cause-and-effect testing, integrated systems testing, and performance verification.

title: Instructional Systems Designer
description:
At Team Carney, we believe that true performance acceleration happens at the intersection of innovative learning and deep strategic expertise. Since 1994, our mission has been to provide top-tier training, learning, and human capital solutions that empower Federal Government agencies to meet their critical mandates. We are seeking a high-performing Instructional Systems Designer (ISD) to support the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) Corporate University (CU) Course Maintenance Program.

This position is contingent on contract award.

Work Schedule and Location

  • Employment Status: Full-Time

  • Location: Remote within the U.S., with anticipated travel to the FDIC Dallas Regional Office (Dallas, TX) approximately once per quarter

Who You Are & What You’ll Do

As an Instructional Systems Designer (ISD) supporting the FDIC Corporate University Course Maintenance Program, you will serve in a Key Personnel capacity responsible for maintaining, revising, and modernizing a comprehensive catalog of professional courses and training collateral. You will work in close collaboration with FDIC Corporate University personnel, Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), and technical monitors to update existing courseware across all instructional delivery formats.

In this role, you will analyze source documentation, review Course Change Sheets, and update learning products across Instructor-Led Training (ILT), Virtual Instructor-Led Training (VILT), Web-Based Training (WBT), Instructional Video, and electronic Job Aids. You will ensure all updated and converted training assets align with Corporate University design standards, templates, style guides, and Section 508 accessibility requirements.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Collaborating closely with FDIC CU personnel, project managers, and SMEs to design, update, and maintain courseware.

  • Updating and revising instructional materials across multiple modalities, including design plans, instructor guides, participant guides, slide decks, case studies, and virtual classroom setups.

  • Reviewing Course Change Sheets and updating content to reflect regulatory, technical, or procedural changes.

  • Developing asynchronous Web-Based Training (WBT) using approved templates and authoring tools (such as Lectora).

  • Creating, scripting, and captioning instructional multimedia, including video files developed in Camtasia (with separate SRT or VTT caption files).

  • Developing and updating electronic performance support tools and job aids in MS Word and PDF formats.

  • Ensuring all deliverables comply with CU technical guidelines, template specifications, and Section 508 accessibility standards.

  • Routing completed deliverables through quality assurance reviews and uploading finalized products to FDIC systems of record and LMS repositories.

What You Bring to the Table - Requirements

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Education, Instructional Design, or a related subject.

  • Experience: Minimum of five (5) years of professional field instructional design experience (excluding time in school).

  • Accessibility Training / Certification: DHS Trusted Tester trained or certified (preferred or able to meet program testing requirements).

  • Demonstrated Functional Experience: Proven, hands-on experience across all of the following core competencies:

    • Technical writing and editing for professional and regulatory audiences.

    • Converting existing and legacy course materials into modern instructional formats.

    • Web-based course development and instructional authoring tools.

    • Multimedia technology integration and visual design.

  • Required Software & Technology Skills:

    • Microsoft Word: Advanced proficiency, including table formatting, custom styles, headers/footers, table of contents creation and updates, page and section breaks, field codes, and working with macros.

    • Microsoft PowerPoint: Advanced proficiency, including slide masters, custom layouts, placeholders, layering, graphic manipulation, and macros.

    • Microsoft Excel: High proficiency in data entry, formatting, sorting, and filtering.

  • Desirable Software & Technology Skills:

    • Lectora Inspire / Lectora Desktop (version 21 or equivalent)

    • Camtasia (video production and closed captioning)

    • Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator)

    • Adobe Connect and Microsoft Teams (virtual training and classroom management)

    • DHS Trusted Tester Section 508 conformance testing processes

Why Join Team Carney?

When you join Team Carney, you join a legacy of excellence. We focus on our people because when we make a positive impact on the lives of our employees, they are able to make a positive impact on our clients. We offer a full suite of competitive benefits, including:

  • Health & Wellness: Multiple medical, dental, and vision insurance options (BCBS CareFirst), health spending accounts (HSA), and flexible spending accounts (FSA).

  • Financial Security: 401(k) retirement plan with company match, plus Carney-paid life and disability insurance.

  • Work-Life Harmony: Generous Paid Time Off (PTO), 11 paid holidays, and 6 weeks of paid parental leave.

  • Professional & Personal Growth: Annual tuition assistance (up to $5,000) and student loan repayment.

  • Get Out and Learn: Up to $200 annually to learn almost anything (from pottery to coding!).

  • Get Out and Run: Up to $200 annually to participate in fitness and active lifestyle events.

  • Continuous Development: Ad hoc training and ongoing professional development access.

  • Analyze market trends and competitive signals to inform investment decisions, capital allocation, and vendor strategy across hyperscale providers, Neo Clouds, edge platforms, and serverless GPU providers

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Extensive knowledge of the product development life cycle, technical design, and data analytics
  • Proven ability to influence the adoption of key product life cycle activities including discovery, ideation, strategic development, requirements definition, and value management
  • Experience driving change within organizations and managing stakeholders across multiple functions

  • Understanding of AI Factory reference architectures and how infrastructure decisions impact performance, cost, scalability, and business outcomes at enterprise scale
  • Experience driving cross-functional alignment across engineering, security, compliance, and lines of business, while building consensus on high-stakes technology, product, and investment decisions
  • Financial acumen to build and articulate AI infrastructure investment strategies, including TCO analysis, depreciation planning, ROI modeling, and multi-year capital planning
  • Demonstrated experience positioning AI infrastructure as a strategic enterprise asset, prioritizing investments across competing demands, and translating evolving AI hardware, architectures, and workload patterns into actionable product strategy
  • Technical depth across the AI infrastructure stack, including AI hardware evaluation, distributed training, real-time inference, workload portability, security, compliance, and regulatory considerations across on-prem, cloud, and hybrid environments

title: Maintenance
description:
Role Overview

The Maintenance Care Partner is responsible for maintaining the physical environment of the community to ensure it remains safe, comfortable, and welcoming for all who live and work there. This includes performing routine inspections, preventive maintenance, repairs, and grounds keeping while responding promptly to service requests. In alignment with the Mission, Vision, and Core Values of our community, this role supports a homelike atmosphere where residents feel a sense of independence, dignity, and belonging. The Maintenance Care Partner recognizes that a well-cared-for environment fosters meaningful connections, engagement, and a thriving community for both residents and care partners.

Key Accountabilities

Conducts daily inspections of the building, grounds, and equipment.
Makes minor adjustments and repairs to heating, cooling, ventilation, plumbing, electrical and lighting systems.
Performs painting and drywall repair duties.
Ensures adherence to Quality Standards, Wellness Strategies and all Health and Safety Regulations.
Maintains a daily maintenance log detailing the work performed.
Reports any noted issues to the Maintenance Supervisor for follow-up.
Responds to repair and maintenance requests in a timely manner.
Performs sidewalk snow removal duties (as required). Keeps all entrances clear and unobstructed. In the absence of a snow removal contract, clears snow from the parking lots (as required).
In the absence of a landscape contract, performs lawn and landscape maintenance duties.
Follows written or verbal instruction from the Maintenance Supervisor.
Collaborates with the Maintenance Supervisor and contractors (as needed).
May be required to move heavy furniture, appliances, equipment, and supplies.
Supports residents in making their living spaces feel like home by ensuring that furniture, decorations, and personal belongings are handled with care and respect.
Collaborates with the Maintenance Supervisor on conducting all scheduled fire drill activities.
Runs the back-up emergency generator monthly to ensure proper operation.
Coordinates the preparation of the resident rooms prior to the arrival of new residents.
Ensures that rooms are welcoming, comfortable, and reflect the unique needs and preferences of each new resident, reinforcing their sense of belonging from day one.
Maintains an up-to-date inventory of supplies and equipment. Reports purchase requests to the Maintenance Supervisor.
Reads and follows manuals, blueprints and other written instructions regarding the proper care and operation of the building systems.
Uses equipment, power tools, and hand tools in a safe and responsible manner.
In the absence of the Maintenance Supervisor, may provide oversite to contracted tradespersons during installations, repairs, and maintenance activities.
Follows weekly/monthly/semi-annual and annual maintenance schedules to ensure optimum building operation and ensures all check sheets are completed and files. For those communities with a computerized maintenance management system (CMMS), logs-in and reviews the maintenance alarm history daily. Checks for proper HVAC system operation and building temperature control and ensures the timely close out of all demand and preventative maintenance work orders.

Required Education

Grade 12 diploma or recognized equivalent is required.
2+ years proven maintenance experience is required.
Certification in building maintenance is considered an asset.

Required Skills

Must have a driver’s license and clean driving record.
A basic understanding of computer literacy is required.
Must be able to communicate effectively and be able to read, write, and speak fluently in the English language.
Must be able to handle the physical demands of the role, including standing, bending, pulling, pushing, climbing, and lifting at least 50 lbs.
Must be able to collaborate with other employees and contacted tradespersons.
Knowledge of Health and Safety practices and Regulations is required.

Additional Education and Skills

Experience in using hand and power tools
Ability to read technical manuals and drawings
Basic knowledge of HVAC, plumbing and electrical systems
Ability to follow instructions and work under pressure with minimal supervision
Proven problem-solving ability skillset is required
Ability to prioritize work loads critical to operations
At least one year of building maintenance experience is preferred

description:
Job Title: Restoration Field Technician

Location: This is an Alberta-based position, in-office or hybrid within the Edmonton or Calgary area.

Company: Silvacom Ltd.

The Role:

You will play a key role in solving complex environmental and land management challenges across Canada. Working within our Energy & Environment team, you will support a diverse portfolio of projects for clients in the municipal, forestry, oil and gas, utility, government, and broader resource sectors. This position combines both field and office responsibilities. You will help carry out habitat restoration and reclamation projects on the ground, from site preparation and planting through to monitoring and data collection. It suits someone who enjoys physical outdoor work, learning restoration techniques in the field, and working closely with project teams, contractors, and equipment operators.

What You'll Do:

Assist with habitat restoration planning, implementation, and monitoring programs
Conduct field assessments and collecting environmental, vegetation, and geospatial data
Assist field operations, equipment operators, and contractors during implementation
Monitor restoration and reclamation sites to track vegetation establishment, survival, and site recovery
Record field observations and prepare technical reports, maps, presentations, and regulatory documentation
Coordinate day-to-day field tasks, schedules, and contractors
Support client engagement and stakeholder communications
Contribute to continuous improvement, innovation, and knowledge development within the team

What you Bring:

Demonstrated interest in habitat restoration, reclamation, or revegetation, with a desire to build field skills
Demonstrated ability and willingness to work safely in remote field environments and varying weather conditions
Experience conducting fieldwork related to forestry, environmental monitoring, restoration, or natural resource projects
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams
Excellent interpersonal, organizational, and communication skills
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
High attention to detail and commitment to producing quality work
Self-motivated with a strong desire to learn and grow professionally
Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced consulting environment
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications
Experience with GIS software (QGIS, ArcGIS, or equivalent) would be considered an asset
Project coordination or project management experience would be considered an asset

Preferred Assets:

Experience working in environmental operations and with equipment operators
Experience with revegetation, planting, seeding, or reclamation work
Silviculture experience
Experience operating ATVs/UTVs, snowmobiles, or other off-road equipment
Valid First Aid certification
Drone pilot certification

Academic Qualifications:

Undergraduate degree or diploma in forestry, environmental science, ecology, natural resource management, environmental planning, agriculture, geography, GIS, or a related discipline
Eligible for or working toward a professional designation such as:

RPF, RPFT, P.Bio., P.Ag., EP, or equivalent

Working Conditions:

Field work may involve travel to project sites across Alberta / Western Canada, including remote locations, for periods of up to 10 days at a time
Fieldwork can involve working in variable weather, walking over uneven terrain, and carrying equipment
Reasonable physical fitness is required for the field portions of the role
A valid Class 5 driver's licence and a satisfactory driver's abstract are required
A company vehicle will be provided for field travel
Overnight stays in field or camp accommodations may be required during active field seasons

Compensation:

We offer competitive salaries commensurate with experience, along with a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a Flexible Spending Account (FSA), and a company-sponsored RRSP plan.

At Bank of America, you can build a successful career with opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact. Join us!

Job Description:

The Special Assets Group (SAG) manages the Bank’s criticized, classified, and distressed commercial credit portfolio. SAG’s primary objective is to maximize recoveries, minimize loss severity, and execute disciplined, risk-based resolution strategies that protect the Bank’s interests while preserving long-term enterprise value where appropriate.

The (SAG) Corp/Comm Senior Portfolio Officer is responsible for managing and resolving the Bank’s most complex criticized, classified, and distressed commercial credit relationships. The Sr. Portfolio Officer develops and executes resolution strategies, leads negotiations with borrowers and stakeholders, and provides subject matter expertise on complex credit situations. This role partners closely with senior leadership, Credit Risk, Legal, and line-of-business partners to drive resolution outcomes that maximize recoveries, minimize losses, and protect the Bank’s interests.

  • Manage a portfolio of highly complex criticized, classified, and distressed commercial credit relationships through all stages of the resolution process.
  • Develop and execute credit resolution strategies designed to maximize recoveries, minimize loss severity, and protect the Bank’s interests.

title: Research & Evaluation Coordinator
description:
About you


We are seeking someone with relevant degree/qualification in evaluation &/or research. Skills in data system management and experience applying data quality and integrity processes for continuous quality improvement. Experience in undertaking evaluation or research with First Nations communities is valuable and the ability to work as part of a collaborative team, operating in Alice Springs, Darwin and Melbourne.


About the role


The Research & Evaluation (R&E) Coordinator will work with the Department Heads to oversight the Evaluation, Monitoring and Research functions of Central Australia. The coordinator will oversee day to day delivery and work in partnership with First Nations leadership groups, Operational Coordinators, staff and communities of Ampe-kenhe Ahehle (Children’s Ground Central Australia).

The coordinator will oversee quality and delivery of daily monitoring and evaluation, in line with Children’s Ground’s longitudinal evaluation frameworks. The focus of our monitoring and evaluation is to evidence the impact of the Children’s Ground Approach and system. Key to this is the data collected as part of our longitudinal evaluation of impact.

The role will coordinate Children’s Ground’s data collection, local processes, quality assurance and control, with oversight and support from the Head of R&E. This includes working across operational teams on data capture, quality, training, reporting and feedback loops. A key part of the role is coordinating and working with First Nations staff and families on the Ampe-kenhe Ahehle triennial evaluation reports and internal annual evaluation reporting and impact reporting.

As the team grows, the R&E Coordinator will manage a small local research and evaluation team to engage with leaders and families in communities to support work with communities to develop community research priorities and projects (when funding and resources are available).

Children’s Ground’s research and evaluation focus on evidencing the impact of the Children’s Ground Approach. Children’s Ground works to ensure communities are designing and leading monitoring, evaluation and research projects and priorities that are important for their own children, families and community, as well as policy priorities.

This role will work closely with staff and families continuing to embed a culture of monitoring and evaluation with all staff and families in the Central Australian region leading Children’s Ground with their communities, as well as staff in achieving high-quality data collection and providing regular data reports and support to use data


Key Responsibilities


Team leadership, supervision and support

· Manage and coordinate day-to-day activity of R&E staff and support them in achieving their priorities

· Ensure all team members have a clear workplan that is reviewed and updated at least quarterly

· Engage in mentoring and learning with First Nations Research staff

· Undertake Children’s Ground’s Quality, Planning, Review & Support (QPRS) process with staff

· Ensure R&E staff are up to date with all organisational compliance and training requirements

· Undertake operational planning with Heads of R&E, R&E staff (and R&E Director)

· Support and contribute to monitoring and evaluation training across the R&E team.

Evaluation reports and data reporting

· Work with First Nations leaders to design and lead the implementation of the Central Australian regional triennial evaluation, in line with Children’s Ground’s longitudinal evaluation frameworks (western and cultural), ethics and standards.

· Work with communities leading the Children’s Ground and Plenty Highway (largely funded by Stronger Communities for Children Australia Government program) to contribute to and undertake evaluation reports as agreed by senior management and the communities.

· Complete regional triennial evaluation reports in a timely manner (within the first year after evaluation period).

· For each regional triennial evaluation period, develop a clear workplan and provide monthly updates to the Heads of R&E, Central Australian Regional Director and other relevant senior managers.

· Work with the Central Australian R&E team and communities to embed internal by-community annual evaluations and quarterly population/community residency status mapping.

· Ensure First Nations staff, leaders and communities are central to all evaluation planning, data collection, analysis, reporting and findings communication.

· Support First Nations leaders and staff to talk with families and communities about our evaluation to ensure they feel informed, empowered and engaged in our data collection and evaluation approaches.

· Engage in peer mentoring – learning from First Nations staff and sharing your knowledge with First Nations and non-First Nations staff.

· Contribute to reflective practice and knowledge development in monitoring and evaluation.

· Contribute to identifying, learning from and sharing national and international best-practice standards in research and evaluation.

High-quality data systems and quality assurance processes

· Oversight and contribute to supporting Area Heads, Directors and staff at all levels to embed a culture of monitoring, evaluation and data informed planning.

· Induct and support new staff of the wider Central Australia team into R&E at Children’s Ground, data system and data input.

· Oversight, monitor and contribute to:

- High quality daily data collection.

- Training in data entry and collection processes and systems (groups and individuals), including meeting regularly with staff over the first month of their employment

- Diverse strategies to ensure regular reminders for all staff about their data collection roles and responsibilities

- Weekly data entry is complete and high-quality for data feedback and reporting purposes

- Weekly data quality and integrity checks and provide feedback to staff on quality and identified gaps.

· Work with senior staff across all CG areas to support embedding CG Enrolment & Consent completion and recording processes.

· Manage, document and communicate staff feedback on the Family Information System.

· Enfranchise First Nations staff in data collection, quality, reporting, communication and ownership.

· Regularly sit with teams, staff and communities to understand their data needs and support their interpretation of the data.

· Lead and contribute to regular reviews of data with staff and communities for use in planning and engagement.

· Regularly reflect on data reporting and sharing processes ensure ongoing quality improvement.

· Work with the team to undertake reflective practice and knowledge development in monitoring and evaluation.

· Contribute to extracting data outputs for quarterly data reports for the organisation, staff, funders and other audiences as needed.

Research and development

· Manage and support on-the-ground logistics of Central Australian research projects, including supporting the team’s engagement with internal or external research partners and projects.

· Contribute to identifying and connecting with research and evaluation partners in relation to Central Australia region.

· Undertake any relevant research data entry, analysis and reporting, if required.

Planning, reporting and other relevant tasks

· Work with the Heads of R&E to contribute to CA team strategic and operational planning.

· Complete written quarterly reports to Heads of R&E about progress, achievements and challenges with research and evaluation.

· Contribute to communicating evidence and impact of the CG Approach, including funding reports, research papers/articles, other publications, conference presentations, evidence reviews, etc, as needed.

· Undertake other monitoring, evaluation and research tasks as needed by R&E Heads and other senior managers.

Local community agency and respect for local cultural knowledge and life

· Encourage and support all First Nations families, valuing their ideas, strategies and aspirations.

· Work with the Community Development team to, where appropriate, meet with local First Nations people and elders to discuss content to inform monitoring, evaluation and research and ensure our approaches do not undermine and actively promote local cultural knowledge and practice.




Key Selection Criteria

Essential skills and experience

· Relevant degree/qualification or relevant experience in evaluation and/or research

· Demonstrated experience in evaluation and research design, development, implementation, data analysis and reporting

· Demonstrated experience in data system management

· Experience in undertaking evaluation or research with First Nations communities

· Knowledge and skills in using Microsoft Word, Excel and Access

· Experience undertaking research and evaluation with communities, preferably First Nations communities

· Experience working alongside First Nations communities

· Excellent verbal and written communication skills

· Ability to plan, organise and prioritise workload around importance and project timelines

· Ability to work cooperatively and collaboratively as a member of the team, and to work autonomously

· Valid Driver’s Licence

· Willingness to undergo a National Police Check and obtain an NT OCHRE Working with Children Check


What we offer

Salary Classification: Children's Ground EBA Level 6- 7 $116,783 - 126,305 (Depending on Skills/Experience) + 12% superannuation + bonus leave

Salary Sacrifice options to increase take home pay (dependant on individual circumstances)

A collaborative, purpose driven organisation contributing to First Nations led systems change


How to Apply

We invite you to walk with us on this unique journey. To apply, please submit your current resume and a cover letter outlining your interest and relevant skills.

The preferred candidate will be required to undertake relevant pre-employment checks, including a National Police Check and Working with Children Clearance (NT).


In line with our workforce development strategy, Children's Ground strongly encourages and supports Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants to apply.

title: Quality Inspector (Starfall)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

QUALITY INSPECTOR (STARFALL)

SpaceX is seeking exceptional employees to enable the success of its Starfall, Dragon, and Starship programs at the Bloomfield, Connecticut site. The Quality Inspector will inspect sewn, cut, and marked soft goods and verification successful execution of critical operations. The Inspector will aid in ensuring high-quality parachute system hardware exists the production line. This role will have a close feedback loop with engineering, production, and the greater SpaceX team in our pursuit of making access to and from space as safe and reliable as possible.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Perform in-process inspections of sewing, stitching, cut parts, and marks using calibrated tools, work orders, and drawings to verify conformance
  • Perform secondary verification of critical work-order operations
  • Perform final inspection of completed soft goods as required; approve or reject hardware and document non-conformances
  • Perform inspection photography of hardware and non-conformances as required
  • Author issue tickets; label nonconforming hardware; track location; assign owners; and follow progress to close
  • Support the Material Review Board (MRB) process by documenting and managing non-conformances
  • Manage calibrated tools: maintain tracking and due dates, remove out-of-tolerance (OOT) equipment from use, disposition OOT with engineering, and ship tools for calibration on time
  • Communicate quality issues with production and engineering and assist with disposition and corrective action
  • Support quality management system (QMS) policies and lean / continuous-improvement activities
  • Inspect parts in accordance with the current drawing revision
  • Help to keep the facility organized; follow FOD, PPE, and material-handling procedures

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience with aerospace soft goods (parachutes, canopies, webbing, industrial sewing, or similar textiles)
  • Experience inspecting industrial sewing, stitching, cut parts, or other textiles / soft goods
  • Experience using inspection tools (scales, micrometers, calipers, cameras)
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, work orders, and specifications
  • Experience using work-order system and documenting non-conformances
  • Knowledge of quality assurance principles, methods, and processes
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook)
  • Strong communication skills (written and oral)
  • Proficiency in other languages (Spanish, Portuguese, Vietnamese)

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be able to work long hours (10+) and weekends/holidays as necessary
  • Must be willing to work all shifts and overtime as needed
  • Must be able to stand for extended periods - 8 hours minimum
  • Able to lift and carry up to 25 lbs. unassisted
  • Must be able to travel to remote sites if required
  • Ability to pass Space Force and Air Force background checks to support travel to Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Software Developer
description:
Job Description

Job Description

Software Developer


Company Overview:

KMS Solutions, LLC is a technical management / solutions company that specializes in engineering, analysis, and cyber security. Founded in 2005, KMS is a certified small business with nearly two decades of experience supporting the Department of Defense as well as many other departments and programs critical to our Nation’s security and well-being.


KMS is a three-time winner of the USA Today Top Workplaces recognizing quality workplace cultures across the United States who put their employees first. Additionally, KMS has won multiple regional Top Workplaces awards and Culture Excellence Awards for Compensation & Benefits, Innovation, Leadership, Purpose & Values and Work-Life Flexibility.


Position Summary

The Software Developer role supports the Marine Species Modeling Team (MSMT) within NUWC Newport’s Ranges, Engineering, and Analysis Department. This position focuses on translating complex mathematical and statistical algorithms into production‑ready Java code, maintaining alignment with engineering design standards, and ensuring algorithmic accuracy critical to environmental compliance modeling and Navy test/training operations. The role requires strong collaboration with MSMT modelers, engineers, and analysts, and includes contributing to broader acoustic modeling, signal processing, and system sustainment efforts.


Essential Functions

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

MSMT Modeling & Algorithm Development

  • Translate and implement mathematical and statistical modeling algorithms from MATLAB into optimized, production‑ready Java code
  • Collaborate with MSMT modelers, acoustic analysts, and senior engineers to validate algorithm behavior, integrate new modeling changes, and ensure scientific accuracy.
  • Apply advanced mathematical concepts—including statistics, Monte Carlo methods, signal processing, and numerical analysis—to support algorithm design, refinement, and performance optimization.
  • Participate in technical design discussions involving data structures, computational efficiency, and model architecture.

Additional Functional Responsibilities

  • Develop, test, debug, and maintain NAEMO and other MSMT software components using Java and modern software engineering principles.
  • Utilize Linux and Windows development environments, command-line tools, and IDEs (e.g., Eclipse) to support full‑stack development workflows.
  • Apply industry best practices such as modular design, version control, code reviews, and unit testing to ensure reliability and maintainability.
  • Implement and optimize data processing routines, databases, and modeling utilities to support Navy test and training analysis.
  • Work within Agile and DevSecOps workflows, contributing to sprint planning, iterative software updates, and secure development pipelines.
  • Produce clear, well‑structured documentation, design artifacts, and software notes to support configuration management and long‑term system sustainment.

Team Dynamics & Work‑Environment‑Driven Functions

  • Operate effectively in NUWC’s highly interactive USB workspace, maintaining productivity amid continuous discussions, fast‑moving priorities, and frequent task re‑alignment.
  • Engage actively with MSMT teammates via Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and other collaboration tools to support real‑time communication and coordination.
  • Use daily software engineering toolsets including Java SE, MATLAB, Eclipse IDE, PowerShell, Git, Spork (GitLab), Jira, Cameo Systems Modeler, and Microsoft 365 applications.
  • Coordinate with engineers, scientists, and analysts to clarify requirements, validate outputs, and ensure alignment between software behavior and mission needs.


Required Education and Experience

  • Ability to obtain a DoD Secret clearance.
  • Bachelor’s Degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Two (2) to five (5) years of professional software development experience.
  • Strong working knowledge of Java; familiarity with MATLAB is highly preferred.
  • Experience using modern development tools (Eclipse, Jira, Spork/GitLab, Git); experience with Cameo Systems Modeler is a plus.
  • Working knowledge of probability, statistics, and general computational concepts.
  • Familiarity with Agile and DevSecOps development practices.


Preferred Education and Experience

  • Active Secret DoD clearance.
  • Master’s Degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related field.
  • Eight (8) years of software engineering experience.
  • Experience supporting U.S. Navy programs, NUWC Division Newport, NAVSEA, or related DoD engineering activities—including undersea warfare systems or Navy test/training operations.
  • Prior military experience in modeling, simulation, training ranges, or marine species/environmental analysis.
  • Experience developing computational algorithms or modeling software for scientific, engineering, or research teams.
  • Experience collaborating with professional software engineers in Agile or DevSecOps environments.
  • Education or hands‑on experience demonstrating comfort with advanced mathematical concepts (statistics, Monte Carlo methods, signal processing) and core computer science topics (data structures, algorithm design).
  • Proficiency with Windows and Linux environments and command‑line tools.
  • Strong understanding of secure development workflows, version control, and modern CI/CD practices.
  • Relevant professional certifications such as Oracle Certified Java Developer (OCP‑JP), MATLAB Certified Programmer, Certified Scrum Developer (CSD), or CompTIA Security+ (CE).


Competencies

  • Strong communication skills (oral and written).
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project).
  • Solid understanding of algorithms, data structures, and computational design principles.
  • Ability to maintain accuracy and attention to detail in fast‑paced, high‑interrupt environments.
  • Proven ability to deliver reliable, maintainable, high‑quality software products.
  • Experience developing software in object‑oriented languages (e.g., Java, Python, C++).
  • Familiarity with modern CI/CD practices and unit testing frameworks.
  • Proficiency with Git version control workflows.
  • Experience working in Linux environments and using command‑line tools.
  • Ability to produce clear, maintainable technical documentation.
  • Strong troubleshooting and debugging skills.


Additional Eligibility Requirements


Work Authorization/Security Clearance Requirement

  • This position requires the ability to obtain and/or maintain a Secret DoD Security Clearance and required access to all worksite locations. Security clearances may only be granted to U.S. citizens.
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and throughout employment.


Other Duties:

Please note this job posting is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.


Supervisory Responsibility:

None


Work Environment:

This position operates in a secure government facility environment. The role involves routine use of computers, secure systems, and standard office/IT equipment. Work is performed on-site at NUWC Division Newport for more than 50% of scheduled hours.

Physical Demands:

Regularly required to talk and hear; frequently required to stand, walk, use hands, and reach with arms. Must be able to lift up to 20 lbs.


Position Type/Expected Hours of Work:

This is a full-time position. The typical workday is eight hours in length. Work hours must align with NUWC’s onsite access schedule, MSMT team collaboration rhythms, and contract requirements. Due to the dynamic and fast-paced nature of MSMT tasking, day-to-day priorities may shift, and the employee must be able to adjust workflow in real time. Flexibility in schedule may be permitted with supervisor approval. Attendance at required onsite meetings, technical discussions, and team working sessions is expected. The employee must account for the full number of hours per pay period necessary to maintain full-time status.


Telework:

  • Telework may be allowed up to 40% after the first six months, subject to customer requirements.


Travel:

  • Ability to travel CONUS; potential OCONUS.
  • Travel up to 10% may be required.


Benefits and Additional Compensation:

KMS offers a competitive benefits packaging including medical, dental and vision insurances, flexible spending account, PTO, paid holidays, military leave, bereavement leave, 401k / retirement savings plan, professional development and tuition reimbursement, basic and voluntary life insurance / AD&D, short-term and long-term disability, voluntary AFLAC supplemental insurance products and employee assistance plan (EAP) program. Additionally, KMS offers employee referral bonuses and a discretionary annual bonus.


AAP/EEO Statement:

KMS Solutions is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer and maintains an Affirmative Action Program. We recruit, employ, train, compensate, and promote qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, genetic information, or any other protected status under applicable federal, state, or local laws. Applicants or employees needing a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process should contact Human Resources.


KMS Solutions is a drug free workplace.

title: Therapist
description:
Project 180 Overview

Mission: SSG-Project 180 provides practical and clinical behavioral health, re-entry, and diversion solutions that empower justice-involved Angelenos to achieve lasting personal transformation and reclaim their lives.

Org. Summary: Project 180 is a leader in the forensic treatment space, offering high-quality, specialized treatment programs that serve thousands of justice-involved individuals. Our programs span criminal justice intercepts and include pre-arrest interventions, court-based diversions, jail in-reach, and intensive post-release services. Project 180 operates in partnership with Los Angeles County agencies including the Department of Mental Health (DMH), the Department of Health Services (DHS), and the Justice, Care and Opportunities Department (JCOD). Annually, we serve over 1,500 justice-involved individuals.

At the heart of our organization are our core values - our fundamental, non-negotiable beliefs that guide how we make decisions and work with one another in service of our mission:

Humanity: We lead with a people-centered focus, seeking to understand and value the lived experience of others and centering their human dignity.

Integrity: We honor the trust placed in us by doing what is right while fulfilling our commitments - even when no one is watching.

Adaptability: We embrace the pivot, evolving to meet the complex needs of our community.

Empowerment: We cultivate the tools, confidence, resilience, optimism, and agency within every individual to lead their own transformation.

Equity: We honor everyone’s unique journey, meet them where they are and commit to providing the targeted support and resources that allow each individual to contribute and thrive.

Interdependence: We move as a unified team, trading silos for collective strength, recognizing that our greatest impact is achieved together.


The Program

The Project Based Housing program is funded by the Department of Health Service (DHS) Office of Diversion and Reentry (ODR), the ODR/ICMS program provides intensive wraparound services to the high-need/high-barrier behavioral health population in the LA County jail system. The program provides permanent supportive housing for some of the most underserved or highest utilizers in the county system. Services are delivered through a recovery-oriented, harm-reduction framework.

The Position

Under the supervision of the Senior Supervisor and Clinical Supervisor, the therapist is responsible for providing intensive, wraparound, field-based clinical services including psychotherapy, rehabilitation, clinical case management, and crisis intervention. Therapists also serve as a member of a multidisciplinary treatment team. A successful Project Based Housing therapist will actively engage this population in services, supporting their clients in making progress towards meaningful recovery goals.

Essential Functions

Provide intensive, wraparound, on-site and field-based clinical services

  • Actively engage clients in services through the development of strong rapport, consistent contact, and use of motivational interviewing. Provide outreach services as needed, meeting clients “where they are at” (service location, client’s point of view).
  • Complete initial assessment, formulate a diagnosis, and engage clients in treatment planning. Services to target symptom reduction and cornerstones of recovery-oriented care (instilling hope, empowerment, self-responsibility, and engaging in meaningful roles).
  • Provide individual and group psychotherapy, rehabilitation, clinical case management and crisis intervention services.
  • Engage and join with collaterals (family members, probation, court) as appropriate. Provide education related to mental health recovery to better support clients. Engage in client advocacy.
  • Service delivery is consistent with ethical standards and a harm reduction, strength-based, trauma-informed framework.

Collaborate with a multidisciplinary treatment team to coordinate client care

  • Actively contributes to the planning and execution of clinical interventions in collaboration with the treatment team. Leverage the unique skills and abilities of team members in service delivery.
  • Participate in outreach and engagement efforts with the treatment team.
  • Coordinate services with various public and private community health, mental health, and social service agencies to ensure appropriate services for clients

Documentation and Reporting

  • Maintain comprehensive case notes in the electronic health record per program guidelines
  • Maintain and submit billing records per program guidelines
  • Participate in program data collection per program guidelines.

Fulfill baseline Project 180 staff expectations.

  • Regular attendance is required. Holiday or weekend work may be required.
  • Maintain and uphold Agency's mission statement, values, policies, procedures, and principles.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor.
  • Maintain active license and/or registrations as applicable (i.e. BBS, CCAPP)

Skills and Abilities

  • Clinical Expertise: Provides clinical care with a focus on high-quality service delivery.
  • Empathetic and able to develop strong relationships with clients
  • Collaborative: Able to work in diverse teams to solve complex issues
  • Adaptive to changing circumstances and client needs in a dynamic environment
  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, remain calm under pressure.
  • Organized: Strong organization systems and attention to detail
  • Communication skills: Clearly conveys information, builds report, and effectively engages with clients.

Minimum Qualification

  • Master’s degree in social work or mental health field from an accredited college or university, and valid license or registration with licensing body (i.e. the BBS).
  • Experience working with culturally diverse populations.
  • Valid CA driver’s license, proof of insurance and own vehicle required.
    • Ability to transport clients in personal vehicle as needed.
  • Must not be on any type of legal supervision (probation or parole).
  • Verification of Employment Eligibility and Background Check
  • Basic computer skills
Preferred
  • Spanish speaking
  • Experience working with forensic and/or dual-diagnosed populations.
  • Experience working on an interdisciplinary team in a mental health or hospital setting.

Supervisory Responsibilities

None

Environmental Conditions (Working Conditions)

Job duties are to be performed both in office and field settings.

Physical Requirements

The employee is expected to move about the worksite throughout the day, which may involve walking, standing, and climbing stairs, or using a mobility device, or similar. The employee is expected to drive, carry a maximum of 20 lbs, listen, and speak in order to complete job requirements.

Mental Requirements

The employee must be able to do any/all of the following: perform complex and varied tasks such as synthesizing information and making decisions without immediate supervision; handle routine distractions, interruptions, noise, and uncontrollable changes in priorities/work schedules; interact professionally and diplomatically in high-stress situations; create and follow plans; meet deadlines.

• Bachelor's degree plus 5 or more years of work experience in a related field.

title: Produktionschef – Sæt retningen for fremtidens forsyning
description:
Produktionschef – Sæt retningen for fremtidens forsyning

Er du klar til at tage ansvar for en samfundskritisk infrastruktur og skabe rammerne for en moderne produktion?

Hos Guldborgsund Forsyning får du, sammen med selskabets øverste ledelse, muligheden for at bygge din egen rolle op, præge strategien og sikre forsyningssikkerheden for hele området. Her får du en hverdag, hvor ikke to dage er ens, og hvor du arbejder tæt sammen med direktionen og dygtige kolleger på tværs af faggrupper.

En koncern i udvikling – med fokus på trivsel og fremtid

Guldborgsund Forsyning er en moderne forsyningskoncern, der leverer fjernvarme og drikkevand samt sikrer effektiv afledning og rensning af spildevand. Vi er 53 engagerede medarbejdere, der sammen omsætter for ca. 320 mio. kr. årligt og gennemfører investeringer og renoveringer for ca. 90 mio. kr. om året. Vores produktion er samlet på Englandsvej 21 i Nykøbing Falster, hvor du får ansvaret for tre produktionslinjer og et team på 22 medarbejdere fordelt på vandselskabet, fjernvarmeselskabet og spildevandsselskabet.

Hos os får du:

  • En udfordrende og spændende hverdag, hvor du arbejder på tværs af faggrupper
  • Mulighed for at præge koncernens udvikling og sikre fremtiden
  • Fokus på balance mellem arbejdsliv og privatliv, trivsel og et sundt arbejdsmiljø
  • Gode udviklingsmuligheder – både fagligt og personligt
  • Flexordning, sundhedsforsikring og attraktive medarbejdervilkår

Sæt dagsordenen for produktionen

Som produktionschef får du en nyoprettet rolle, hvor du sammen med direktionen sætter dagsordenen for produktionen. Du får ledelsesansvar for tre teamledere og skal implementere strategiske målsætninger, bidrage med input til det strategiske arbejde og sikre forsyningssikkerhed, driftsøkonomi og beredskab på tværs af selskaberne. I starten handler det om at skabe rammerne for arbejdet, standardisere processer og sikre, at ressourcer og mandskab kan bruges på tværs. Du skal skabe en ensartet ledelsesstruktur og metoder, der bygger på vores værdier: værdibærer, genkendelig, pålidelig og ansvarlig.

Du kommer også til at arbejde med grøn omstilling, NIS2, GDPR og FN’s verdensmål – uden at du behøver være ekspert. Over tid vil myndighedsarbejde og samarbejde med eksterne parter fylde op til 20% af din hverdag. Du bidrager til styregrupper for projektporteføljer, arbejdsmiljø og samarbejdsudvalg, og du deltager i faste møder med direktionen, konferencer og besøg på lokationer.

Dine primære opgaver

Du får en varieret hverdag, hvor du:

  • Har det overordnede ansvar for forsyningssikkerhed, driftsøkonomi og beredskab på tværs af tre produktionsselskaber
  • Implementerer strategiske målsætninger og bidrager til strategisk udvikling
  • Skaber rammerne for arbejdet og standardiserer processer på tværs af produktionslinjer
  • Sikrer en ensartet ledelsesstruktur og metoder, der bygger på virksomhedens værdier

title: Director, Operational Deal Services - Interpath Advisory
description:
Director, Operational Deal Services
Value Creation
London, United Kingdom

Interpath is a fast-growing international advisory firm with deep expertise across deals, value creation, advisory, and restructuring. We help global businesses, investors, and stakeholders navigate complexity, make critical decisions, and deliver measurable results. Agile, independent, and conflict-free, we are driven by a commitment to doing what's right - every time.

Our diverse teams combine specialist technical capability with deep sector knowledge. Since launching in 2021, we have expanded rapidly across the UK, Ireland, France, Algeria, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Spain, BVI, Cayman Islands, Bermuda, Barbados, India, South Africa, Singapore, and Hong Kong. Now with the backing of Bridgepoint Private Equity, our ambition is clear: to be one of the world's leading advisory firms with a truly global footprint by 2030.

About the Value Creation Team
Interpath's Value Creation practice is a high-growth, international team delivering impactful, results-driven programmes for listed corporates, private equity funds, large corporates, and government bodies. Our Value Creation service line consists of 6 pillars of expertise, Performance Improvement, Procurement & SCM, Operational Deal Services, Strategy, Technology Data & AI and Turnaround.

We support global clients who need to improve performance, unlock value, and accelerate transformation and we use data-driven insights to diagnose issues, identify opportunities & deliver sustainable performance improvement. Our client projects have wide-ranging operational delivery & impact on business areas including sales, manufacturing, supply chain management,?logistics &?purchasing.

Projects include:

  • Operational Due Diligence
  • Helping clients to assess risk
  • Planning integration or separation
  • Cost reduction
  • Revenue enhancement
  • Day-1 readiness and 100-day planning
  • Delivering value after completion

The Opportunity
Following the appointment of several new Managing Directors, we are expanding rapidly and seeking talented individuals to help drive our ambitious growth plans.

As a Director, you will;
  • Build and develop a network across Private Equity and Corporates, identifying opportunities to assist clients and deliver tailored solutions;
  • Complete sell side & buyside operational due diligence, post-merger integration/ separation projects, performance improvement, cost reduction, revenue enhancement, Day-1 readiness and 100-day planning;
  • Own & drive workstreams including scoping, report development & delivery of findings;
  • Oversee the preparation of high-quality client materials including analysis packs, diligence reports, workstream updates & presentations;
  • Execute robust methodologies to ensure clarity, ownership, and delivery to tight timescales and to mitigate risks;
  • Coach and mentor junior colleagues, helping them to develop strong analytical, consulting & deal delivery skills, contributing to their professional growth???
  • Support business development activity, including proposal development, credentials, sector research, target analysis, and preparation of pitch materials;
  • Enhance delivery quality and strengthen Interpath's market reputation

Successful candidates will benefit from:
  • Continuous professional development
  • Deep technical and commercial expertise
  • Direct exposure to C-suite stakeholders
  • Experience delivering complex, high-impact change
Requirements

We are looking for individuals with:
  • Proven experience in diagnosing, and delivering performance improvement consulting projects, pre & post deal
  • A track record of delivering operational value creation, improvement or transformation mandates
  • Strong financial and operational analytical skills and the ability to conduct deep-dive analysis and build complex financial models and operational methodologies/ approaches
  • Excellent academic record including previous experience at a leading advisory firm, a Big 4 or a company undergoing significant deals transformation activities
  • Professional, with the ability to engage effectively with clients in high-pressure situations
  • Flexibility to travel when required for client engagements?
Benefits

At Interpath, our people lie at the heart of our business. That's why we provide employees with a competitive and comprehensive reward package including compelling salaries and a range of core and optional benefits. Read more about our benefits; Company Benefits - Interpath

Unsolicited Resumes from Third-Party Recruiters
Please note that Interpath do not accept unsolicited resumes from third-party recruiters. Any employment agency, person or entity that submits an unsolicited resume does so with the understanding that Interpath will have the right to hire that applicant at its discretion without any fee owed to the submitting employment agency, person or entity.

title: Parachute Rigger & Quality Specialist (Starfall)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

PARACHUTE RIGGER & QUALITY SPECIALIST (STARFALL)

SpaceX is seeking exceptional employees to enable the success of its Starfall and Dragon parachute systems. The Parachute Rigger & Quality Specialist will pack parachutes in accordance with documented procedures across several products. Additionally, this role will assist in reviewing the quality and conformance of numerous other soft goods components that the Bloomfield, Connecticut site produces. This role will have a close feedback loop with engineering, production, and the greater SpaceX team in our pursuit of making access to and from space as safe and reliable as possible.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Fold, rig, and pack parachutes for both human and cargo spaceflight in accordance with SpaceX policies and procedures
  • Support development of new packing/rigging procedures for new projects
  • Support continuous improvement of work instructions and procedures
  • Perform build reviews and drive improvements to product quality and reliability
  • Perform in-process inspections, final inspections, and post-flight inspections of parachutes and other soft goods, identifying and documenting non-conformances according to SpaceX policies and procedures
  • Inspection methods include visual inspection and use of scales and micrometers
  • Validate incoming parts and materials to approved drawings and specification standards. Create record of the quality review
  • Maintain and promote a quality culture within the organization
  • Manage calibrated equipment and testing equipment, including coordinating on-time re-calibration

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate
  • 2+ years of inspection or technician experience in an aerospace, military, or manufacturing environment

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Strong communication skills (written and oral)
  • Senior Riggers License - FAA (Federal Aviation Administration) or military equivalent
  • Experience with parachute systems (large or cargo canopies preferred, and/or pressure packing canopies)
  • Experience with textiles (cord, webbing, tape, broadcloth, and thread) and the ability to interpret technical drawings
  • Experience in a quality department or in quality training
  • Experience with high-consequence, meticulous procedural work (e.g., FAA Airframe and Powerplant (A&P) certificate or similar)
  • Knowledge of quality assurance principles, methods, and processes
  • Experience with high-resolution inspection photography
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook)
  • Experience with hydraulic equipment, ovens, hand tools, and tension testing
  • Proficiency in other languages (Spanish, Portuguese, Vietnamese)

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be able to work long hours (10+) and weekends/holidays as necessary
  • Must be able to stand for extended periods - 8 hours minimum
  • Must be willing to work all shifts and overtime as needed.
  • Must be able to travel to remote sites if required.
  • Able to lift and carry up to 25 lbs. unassisted
  • Ability to pass Space Force and Air Force background checks to support travel to Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Software Engineer
description:
About the Role

This is a full-stack software engineering role at a seed-stage AI platform company serving the hospitality industry, where AI agents handle guest communication and operations workflows at scale. You'll own meaningful pieces of the AI system end-to-end, from intent classification and knowledge retrieval through tool orchestration and response generation. The engineering team is flat, giving you real autonomy over design decisions and the systems you build.

What You'll Do

  • Design and build response generation pipelines, including routers, orchestrators, and synthesizers that classify intent, assemble context, select tools, and decide when to send or escalate.

  • Develop knowledge retrieval systems that ground agent responses in accurate, current data despite messy real-world inputs.

  • Build tool orchestration layers that execute multi-step workflows reliably, including graceful handling of third-party API failures mid-conversation.

  • Create evaluation frameworks that measure quality against real conversations and catch regressions before they reach customers.

  • Implement observability and tracing that makes agent reasoning legible and trustworthy to non-technical support teams.

  • Design controls and interfaces that let support leads adjust agent behavior without writing code.

  • Extend the system to voice conversations with real-time transcription and the same tool-use capabilities as text.

  • Optimize for speed and cost through model routing, caching, and prompt refinement.

  • Own infrastructure, data pipelines, integrations, and API work that underpin the platform.

What We're Looking For

  • 3 or more years of experience building and shipping production systems that real users depend on.

  • Experience designing and debugging AI/ML systems in production, including retrieval pipelines, prompt engineering, or model orchestration.

  • Proficiency across multiple layers of the stack: backend, frontend, infrastructure, or data pipelines.

  • Experience building and evaluating retrieval systems such as knowledge bases, ranking, context validation, or semantic search.

  • Experience designing multi-step workflows, tool orchestration, or function-calling systems.

  • Experience building observability, tracing, or debugging tools for complex pipelines.

  • Proficiency in at least one backend language such as Python, Go, Rust, or Java.

  • Experience integrating with third-party APIs and handling failure modes in production.

  • Bonus: experience with real-time or low-latency systems, voice and transcription, model routing, or building configuration interfaces for non-technical users.

  • Candidates must be authorized to work in the US (no visa sponsorship).

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base salary: $130,000 to $220,000 annually

  • Equity: 0.20% to 1.20%

  • Comprehensive health insurance and 401(k) match

Location

On-site in San Francisco, CA. This is not a remote role.

title: ETL Database Developer
description:
The ETL/Database Developer will play a crucial role in the continued effort of designing, implementing, and optimizing our company infrastructure while collaborating with cross-functional teams to deliver meaningful data solutions. title: Principal Machine Learning Engineer
description:
About the team

The Security and Risk Engineering organization builds scalable, AI-powered security solutions that reduce risk and protect ServiceNow and its customers. We value AI-first thinking, clean architecture, intuitive experiences, and a culture of continuous learning.

This is a zero-to-one incubation. We’re building a new class of exposure analysis that ranks security work by exploitability—where an attacker could realistically get in—rather than raw severity. The architecture is evolving, and this role helps define what good looks like.

The role

As a Principal ML Engineer, you set the technical vision for exploitability-based security across the portfolio—not just one engine. You define the hardest modeling problems worth solving, set the direction other staff and senior engineers build within, and represent the work to executives, customers, and the broader engineering organization.

What you’ll own

  • The technical vision and architecture for exploitability-driven security: where the engine goes next, and the class of problems it should solve beyond any single release.
  • The hardest unsolved modeling problems—how calibrated attack-path probability holds up across environments, how identity and agent surfaces enter the model, and how ground truth feeds back into it.
  • The engineering standards and architectural direction that multiple teams build within: scalability, reliability, and the scientific rigor of the scoring.
  • The build-on strategy across the portfolio: what the engine reuses from existing products, what must be net-new, and why.

What you’ll do

  • Set technical direction across multiple teams without direct authority, and turn ambitious ideas into working, enterprise-grade products.
  • Explore and apply emerging AI to cybersecurity in fundamentally new ways—not simply bolt AI onto existing products.
  • Represent the team’s technology and innovation with executives, customers, partners, and the broader engineering organization.
  • Mentor staff and senior engineers, and raise the overall engineering bar through coaching and technical leadership.
  • Champion AI-native engineering practices, including extensive use of coding agents and autonomous development, testing, evaluation, and operational workflows.
  • Set the direction for AI safety, security, governance, and guardrails for agentic systems running in production.

What you bring

  • Deep expertise in modern AI/ML with a track record of building production AI systems—LLMs, foundation models, agentic architectures, RAG, retrieval, and model evaluation—alongside probabilistic or ML-driven scoring.
  • The ability to set a compelling technical vision and drive it across teams, then go deep into architecture and code.
  • A proven record of turning ambitious, ambiguous ideas into products that scale to enterprise workloads.
  • An innovator’s mindset—challenging conventional approaches and seizing the openings created by rapidly evolving AI.
  • Command of distributed systems, APIs, cloud-native platforms, and data or graph systems.
  • Expert-level Python and modern AI frameworks and infrastructure; experience with Java, Go, or similar languages is valuable.
  • Executive-level communication: able to articulate a compelling technical vision to engineers, customers, and senior leadership.
  • Applied depth in security problems—threat detection, vulnerability and exposure management, identity security, risk prioritization, or autonomous remediation—is strongly preferred.
  • Extensive use of AI-native development tools and coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Windsurf across the software development lifecycle.

  • 15+ years of software engineering experience, including significant technical and engineering leadership responsibility.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and delivering AI/ML-powered products and platforms in production.
  • Experience leading technical initiatives spanning multiple teams without direct authority.
  • Demonstrated ability to design systems that scale to enterprise workloads.
  • Hands-on experience with frontier LLMs, agent frameworks, retrieval and vector technologies, and model evaluation and observability; probabilistic modeling or graph analytics is a strong plus.
  • Strong backend engineering experience with distributed systems, APIs, microservices, and cloud-native architectures.
  • Extensive experience using AI-native development tools and coding agents as part of the software development lifecycle.
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Cybersecurity products, or deep familiarity with modern security architectures and security operations, is strongly preferred.

title: Avionics Systems Engineer (Falcon & Dragon)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

AVIONICS SYSTEMS ENGINEER (FALCON & DRAGON)

As a systems engineer in Falcon & Dragon Avionics, you will have the unique opportunity to be part of a cross functional team of engineers that bridge the gap between vehicle analysis, design, and production extending through vehicle operations. You’ll be part of a team that owns a wide scope, combining mechanical, electrical and software engineering practices to enable an unprecedented launch rate while maintaining a high reliability to ensure mission success.

Your creativity and relentless commitment to quality will be expected to analyze systems designs, define new processes, develop system validation techniques and introduce new designs in order to improve vehicle performance, bring down cost and sustain an aggressive launch rate for the leading launch vehicle in the world. You will also put your engineering knowledge to the test by performing real-time troubleshooting on the vehicle as it goes from the integration phase through launch operations. Our fundamental goal is to allow humanity to explore the stars; with it comes extreme responsibility to ensure the safety of the crew and payload.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Represent the Falcon & Dragon avionics system throughout all stages of integration, from production and test all the way through launch and refurbishment
  • Troubleshoot issues on prototype and production assemblies on an aggressive production schedule
  • Work collaboratively with other teams and customers to define the scope of development projects and initial product requirements as new designs move from concept, through prototype, and into production
  • Develop tools and processes to support an unprecedented launch rate
  • Perform design and manufacturing assessments of new designs and drive optimization for manufacturability, quality, and cost
  • Be the lead on system projects including creation, maintenance, and communication of development schedules with sufficient detail to ensure that all assigned personnel are aware of theirs tasks and deadlines as well as identify internal and external resources required to support the project
  • Develop, execute, and document the avionics system verification on flight and flight-representative hardware at the system-level and validate the as-built vehicle is “go for launch"

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in an engineering field, science or math
  • 1+ years of experience using software tools such as Matlab, C++ or Python
  • 1+ years of experience with electrical component design, system level integration of electronic components or system level testing

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Software fluency, enabling automation of test or analysis tasks and manipulation of large data sets
  • Experience with wire harnesses and associated sub-components
  • Experience with 3D CAD software
  • Experience installing and troubleshooting various electronic sensors and components.
  • Competence with electrical test equipment (multimeters, oscilloscopes, power supplies, etc.)
  • Creative problem solver that can bring multiple disciplines together with the ability to assess risk and make design and development decisions without all available data
  • Self-motivated with strong multi-tasking, organizational, communication and documentation skills
  • Strong sense of accountability and integrity with excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to work in a fast paced, autonomously driven, and demanding atmosphere

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Extended hours and weekend work may be required to support critical project and mission milestones
  • Minimal travel will be required

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
