title: Senior DevOps Engineer - Mainloop
description:
Senior DevOps EngineerBuild a company's entire delivery platform from the first commit, own it outright, and never carry a pager.

No deje pasar esta oportunidad, inscríbase rápidamente si su experiencia y habilidades coinciden con lo que se indica en la siguiente descripción.

Both halves of that sentence are deliberate.This is a senior role and it is not a role we can hire junior into — you are the first, for a while the only, and the platform everyone else builds on is the one you put in place.Mainloop is a new engineering team inside an established international group.

We are in Barcelona, we are being built from scratch this year, and we have the backing, the customers and the product portfolio of a company that has been around for decades.

You get the interesting part of a new team without the part where you check whether payroll clears.Two more things about where this comes from and where it goes.

The group has been running a tech lab in Casablanca for more than eight years — Barcelona is its second, built to sit closer to the teams we build for, and AI-native from the first commit, because it starts from a blank page.

And the plan does not stop at internal work: within about a year and a half we intend to externalise — external clients, our products sold on the market, products developed for it.

The first eighteen months are deliberately spent building as much as possible for the group while the machine gets set up.

You would arrive at the start of that curve, not after it.What we build is the software that automates professional-services work — across roughly fifteen countries, for businesses drowning in process.

We build those products and we run them.

That second half is why this role exists, and it is not a formality: a team that owns how its software is built should own how it ships.You are the person who ends that.

You are our first DevOps engineer, and for a while our only one.What the job actually isYou are not inheriting a platform.

You are writing one.There is no infrastructure-as-code in our estate today — not a line.

The environments that exist were built by hand and are reconstructible only from a runbook and one person's memory.

Your first job is to make that permanently untrue: every environment we run reproducible from a committed repo, from your first week, before the habit sets.In your first few months you will:Build the platform from code.

Hosts, networking, ingress, access, environments — committed, parameterised, reviewable.

It is the cheapest moment this will ever be done, and you get to do it properly instead of retrofitting it.Make deployment self-serve.

Today, shipping an existing app is a git push; standing up a new one needs admin rights and two undocumented footguns.

That gap is yours to close, down to one command, so a developer never holds a platform credential.Own secrets properly.

A real machine secrets manager, and — because we run a lot of AI agents — credentials brokered so an agent process only ever holds a placeholder, never a key.

If you have opinions about how you stop a prompt-injected agent leaking a production credential, you will enjoy this part; almost nobody gets to design it from scratch.Prove the restore.

We have a written standard that says "someone deploys it" is not "someone has proven the restore works." You will run the drill, write the report, and be the reason the honest answer to "is it backed up?" changes from no to yes, and here is the evidence.Build the release path.

Commit to production, an automated test gate, per-branch preview URLs a stakeholder can open from their phone, and a rollback that everyone on the team has rehearsed before they need it.Then keep it all running — and keep making it duller.

Observability, cost caps, dependency hygiene, the unglamorous work that decides whether a small team can own a lot of products.And you will have the authority to match.

You are not implementing someone else's platform design.

You report directly to Edouard, there is no layer in between, and how this is built is yours to decide.

We are hiring at senior level precisely so that those decisions can be yours — the platform every product here runs on is the one you put in place, and we would rather bring in the judgement than supervise it.Nobody is on call.

Ever.No rota, no pager, no phone number, no "just keep an eye on it this weekend".

Alerts post to a team channel and wait there.

If something breaks at 3am on a Saturday, or in the second week of August, it gets fixed the next working morning.

This is a decision on the record, not an oversight we will rediscover later — and it applies to every product we own, with no exceptions.We are telling you this up front because it is not a perk we are quietly hoping you will waive.

Plenty of ads say "healthy on-call culture" and mean a rota.

We mean there is no rota.Here is the honest other half, and it is the actual job: we can only make that promise because we protect ourselves with engineering instead of with people's evenings — and that engineering is what we are hiring you to build.

Infrastructure as code, so a lost machine is rebuilt rather than resurrected.

Backups with a restore we have actually tested.

A rollback that is one click and that everyone has already practised.

Alerting that queues instead of paging, because nothing on the other end of it is expected to answer at night.So the trade is explicit: you are never woken up, and in exchange the systems have to be genuinely recoverable.

If you have spent a career being paged for things that should have been engineered away, this is the version of the job where you get to do the engineering instead.During working hours it is the opposite of hands-off.

The PO, the developers and the DevOps engineer assigned to a product own that product's incidents — support is not shipped off to a separate team, it is part of owning the thing, and it is what keeps everyone honest about quality.How we build — deliberately boring, and you get a say in itWe have a settled stack and it is the same in most repos on purpose: one scaffold, shared packages, push-to-deploy.

The payoff is that a two-person team can pick up a product they have never seen and be useful the same day, which is the only reason a team this size can own this many products.We build the simplest platform that meets the requirement, and we are strict about what the requirement actually is.

Complexity here has to earn its place: every capability we run is one more thing one team has to understand, patch and be able to rebuild.A concrete example, because it tells you a lot about us: we do not run Kubernetes, and that was a decision rather than an omission.

We looked at it properly, twice — most recently because we were worried we had got it wrong — and both times the answer was that a small portfolio on predictable traffic does not need multi-node scheduling and autoscaling badly enough to pay for them with the only infrastructure engineer we have.

We wrote down the specific conditions under which we would change our minds, and when one of them is met, we will.Which is why we are asking for someone who has run Kubernetes in production and can tell us when it is not the answer.

If your idea of a good week is tuning a cluster, this is the wrong job and we would rather you knew now.

If your idea of a good platform is one a small team can fully understand, rebuild from a repo and hand to a new joiner in an afternoon — and you have enough scar tissue to know where that stops being enough — that judgement is most of what we are hiring.It is a default, not a straitjacket.

Some things genuinely need something else, and when they do we adapt deliberately, with the reasoning written down.

What we do not do is re-decide the same five questions on every new repo out of habit.And you get a say in what the standard is.

Anyone can propose a change — something new that is genuinely better, something we should upgrade to, something we got wrong.

A proposal gets researched properly against the alternatives, it gets an answer, and if the answer is no you get the reasoning.

On infrastructure, you are not one voice among many — you are the one who decides, within a budget you help set.You will get seriously good at building with AI agentsWe are an AI-native engineering team, genuinely — not a team that added a Copilot licence.

Every engineer gets their own Claude Max subscription and a desktop orchestrator that runs several coding agents in parallel, each in its own branch.

That is true of you too: a great deal of infrastructure work is now specified rather than typed, and you will get very good at driving that — where it works, where it fails, and how to read a diff and decide whether it is actually right.It also makes your job more interesting than the same title elsewhere, because agentic engineering creates infrastructure problems most teams do not have yet:Agents install packages into code that sits next to client data.

Supply-chain hygiene stops being a compliance checkbox and becomes a live control you own.Agents hold credentials — or rather, they must not.

Brokering machine identity so the agent never touches the real key is a design problem, and it is yours.Agents cost money in a way that is invisible until the invoice.

Per-project budgets, hard caps and an alert that fires before the cap, not after it.Agents can deploy.

Which means the guardrails between "an agent proposed this" and "this is in production" are infrastructure, not policy.If you have been running agents seriously and have opinions about where they break, we want to hear them.

If you are curious but not yet deep in it, that is fine — teaching this well is something we intend to be known for.The Mainloop Barcelona certificateSomething we are building alongside the team, and we think it is genuinely unusual.Over your first two to three years here you work through a defined body of knowledge — our architecture, the agentic build method, how to take a product from an idea to something a business depends on, and how to run it well.

When you have covered it and can demonstrably run a project our way, you are awarded the Mainloop Barcelona certificate.It is yours.

It goes on your CV, and we intend to make it mean something in this market — a signal that the person holding it knows how to build and run production software with AI agents to a standard.

We are investing in making it prestigious, because a team whose alumni are sought after is a team good people want to join.If you would be moving countries to take this job, this is the part to weigh most carefully.

You would not only be taking a role; you would be spending two or three years acquiring a way of building and running systems that the market is currently repricing upward — and leaving with something you can show for it, on top of a platform you can point at and say you built.Things worth knowing up frontThis is an on-site role in Barcelona.

More than the other seats here, and for a real reason: you are standing up physical-ish infrastructure and access for a team being assembled around you, in its first year, and most of that goes faster in a room.You are the only DevOps engineer for a while.

That is authority, and it is also a bus factor — which is why "nothing exists only in one person's head" is written into the role rather than hoped for.

Everything you build gets documented and reproducible as you go, not afterwards.We are building the team this year, and you will shape how it works.

Some of our processes are written, some are not, and the ones written after you arrive will have your fingerprints on them.If you would be moving to Barcelona for thisWe do not expect you to absorb the cost of relocating, and we would rather say what we cover than leave you to ask.We pay to get you here.

Flights, your first month's accommodation while you find somewhere of your own, the visa and paperwork costs, and an agent to handle the bureaucracy — the NIE, the TIE appointment, the apostilles — instead of leaving you to meet the Spanish administrative system alone.

Spanish lessons if you want them.A relocation bonus, paid on arrival rather than dripped out.

It is repayable only if you leave within the first eighteen months, and that condition is the reason we can pay it up front — moving countries costs money at the start, not in year two.Three things here are worth more than they look on an offer comparison, particularly against a US one:Nobody is on call.

Ever.

It has its own section above and we mean it literally.

If you are coming from a market where infrastructure work and a pager are assumed to travel together, read that section twice — it is the single largest difference between this job and the same title elsewhere, and it is not a perk we are quietly hoping you will waive.Healthcare with no premium, no deductible and no network — from day one, and not tied to staying in this job.Thirty calendar days of holiday — that is 22 working days — plus fourteen public holidays, roughly seven weeks in total.

That is the statutory floor in Spain, not a benefit we are being generous with.And the on-site line reads differently depending on where you are standing.

For someone already in Barcelona it is a constraint and we have said why.

For someone moving here it is most of the point: this is a job in Barcelona, not a job you do from Barcelona — a team that sits together, in a city worth being physically present in.If you are coming from the United States, two things are usually worth more than the headline salary gap and almost nobody has done the arithmetic: a salary here can sit below the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion, and federal student loans on an income-driven plan are assessed on the income that exclusion has already removed.

We are not your tax advisor and you should get one — but ask in the first conversation and we will walk you through the comparison we ran, including the parts where the number comes out smaller.What we are looking forRead this as a description of the engineer you will be here, not a checklist you have to arrive with.

Almost nobody ticks all of it on day one, and we would rather hire someone with the instinct and train the rest — that is a large part of what the certificate is for.You have built infrastructure from nothing before, and it survived other people using it.

A platform you were handed and maintained is fine; a platform you created is what we are asking for.

This is the one non-negotiable, and it is why the role is senior: there is nobody here to check your work, and the platform you put in place is the one everyone else builds on for years.Infrastructure-as-code is how you work, not a tool you have used.

You can talk about what you do when reality and the repo disagree, because it always eventually does.You have owned backups and actually restored from them — under time pressure, ideally when it mattered.

Everyone has backups.

Far fewer have restored.You are comfortable running things on your own servers, not only on a managed cloud console.

We own our infrastructure deliberately, and that is a different skill from configuring somebody else's.You have run Kubernetes in production — and you are equally comfortable saying when it is not the right answer.

We do not run it today.

Whether and when we do is one of the decisions this job owns, and we would rather that call were made by someone who has lived with the thing than by someone reasoning about it from the outside.You automate yourself out of the loop, and you write things down.

The measure of this job is how little of it requires you specifically.You can say no to complexity.

The best engineer for this seat is the one who builds the boring thing that works and resists the interesting thing that does not need to exist.Security is instinct, not a stage.

Secrets, access, least privilege, patching — the boring disciplines, held consistently.English, fluently.

It is our working language — we work across roughly fifteen countries.

Spanish is genuinely useful day to day.

Catalan is not required.Barcelona.

This is a team that sits together, especially in its first year.We do not care what you studied.

We care what you have built and run, and whether you can talk us through the decisions in it.How we hireOur process is unusual, so here it is up front.

Four rounds, and none of them is a puzzle.Fifteen minutes with Edouard.

A short first conversation — who you are, what you are after, and what this actually is.

Enough for both of us to work out whether the next one is worth an hour.A thirty-minute conversation.

What you have built, how you work, and how you think about it.

We will ask you to walk us through something you built and then to justify a specific decision inside it.

There is no way to prepare for that and it is not meant to catch you out; it is how we tell understanding from familiarity.A conversation with our Casablanca team.

The group has run a tech lab there for more than eight years.

You get people who have run production at real scale asking their own questions — and you get to ask them yours, including the ones you would rather not ask the person hiring you.A project.

We give you a brief and a working environment to build it in, with Claude Code already set up and wired to a key, so you are building the way we actually build rather than talking about it at a whiteboard. xqbhyrx

It is real work rather than a puzzle, you do it on your own schedule — no week off, no flights, nothing that requires you to already be free — and we go through what you built together afterwards.

title: Project Supplier Quality Representative
description:

Extraordinary teams building inspiring projects:

Since 1898, we have helped customers complete more than 25,000 projects in 160 countries on all seven continents that have created jobs, grown economies, improved the resiliency of the world's infrastructure, increased access to energy, resources, and vital services, and made the world a safer, cleaner place.

Job Summary:

In this role, you will prepare supplier quality procedures, operating instructions and develop project specific metrics. You will issue assignments for quality surveillance, capability surveys, and audits. You will plan and oversee surveillances, report technical and quality issues, and monitor dispositions and corrections.

Major Responsibilities:

  • Advises interested parties of technical and quality issues reported in area/shop Quality Surveillance Reports

  • Participates in resolution of technical and quality issues arising from area/shop Supplier Quality activities
  • Participates in preparation of project corrective actions and root cause analyses to resolve significant issues that represent immediate or potential impact to the project

A Bachelor's degree in Engineering from a reputed University. Minimum 6 plus years of relevant industry experience in inspection and testing activities. Basic computer skills including Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Power Point).Experience in Renewables, Pipeline, Petrochemical, Refining, LNG, Renewable Energy, Fracking, Heat treatmentPrevious in shop quality surveillance or related experiencePrevious experience in planning inspections and tests

ADDITIONAL QUALIFICATIONS:A minimum of 2000 hours of in-shop quality surveillance or related work. Must be a US Citizen.

Required Knowledge and Skills:

    • Experience with major commodities typically procured for Energy projects, recognized codes and standards, manufacturing methods
    • Performs project Supplier Quality functions having some degree of complexity, e.g., preparation of detailed inspection plans for use on complete or uniquely designed systems; preparation of full scope man-hour and budget estimates for proposed intermediate-sized projects; review of complex technical specifications; or the establishment of project corrective action(s) to resolve nonconformances that have a significant impact on project cost/schedule

    Conducts capability surveys of a prospective supplier

Total Rewards/Benefits:

For decades, Bechtel has worked to inspire the next generation of employees and beyond! Because our teams face some of the world's toughest challenges, we offer robust benefits to ensure our people thrive. Whether it is advancing careers, delivering programs to enhance our culture, or providing time to recharge, Bechtel has the benefits to build a legacy of sustainable growth. title: Central Maintenance Service Coordinator
description:
The Dolese Promise is built on a foundation of integrity driven by our passion for quality, safety, and reliability. We are one of Oklahoma's most respected employee-owned companies because of our people and our values. We strongly believe in positively impacting our communities through our products, our actions, and our financial support.

Being a part of the Dolese team affords a unique opportunity to join an organization that rewards its owners through profit sharing. Our employees are one of our most important resources, which is why we promise to deliver.

Dolese Delivers:

  • Stable Foundation
  • Treat with Respect
  • Safe Environments
  • Employee Focus

JOB SUMMARY

Grow your career with a company built on Safety, Integrity, Teamwork, and Stewardship. As a CMS Service Coordinator at Dolese, you will coordinate fleet maintenance workflow activities through the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS). This role serves as a key point of coordination between maintenance shops, field locations, and technicians to help ensure preventive maintenance, repairs, and inspections are completed on time with minimal disruption to operations. In this role, you will proactively schedule maintenance activities, track upcoming service needs, assist with parts procurement, create purchase orders, and help maintain accurate maintenance records while supporting overall shop efficiency.

WHY JOIN US

We are people, building communities from the ground up. For our employees, we are focused on building careers. Joining our team means:

  • Stability & Legacy: Be part of a company with more than a century of success, operational excellence, and a strong commitment to our employees.

  • Growth Opportunities: Expand your skills in maintenance coordination, scheduling, and operational support while gaining experience working with maintenance personnel, vendors, and field operations teams.

  • Impactful Work: Your contributions help ensure maintenance activities are coordinated effectively, supporting fleet reliability, equipment availability, and efficient maintenance operations.

  • Supportive Culture: Our employees support one another and our customers through our service values: Champion Kindness, Incite Enthusiasm, Build Relationships, and Provide Innovative Solutions. We value collaboration, integrity, and continuous improvement.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES/ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Maintenance Coordination

  • Manage daily maintenance workflow activities through the CMMS.

  • Review, prioritize, and coordinate incoming repair requests and work orders.

  • Coordinate shop schedules to maximize technician productivity.

  • Schedule preventive maintenance services based on mileage, hours, or time intervals.

  • Schedule and coordinate mobile service work at plant and jobsite locations.

  • Monitor work order status and support timely completion of maintenance activities.

  • Follow up on overdue work orders and outstanding repairs.

Communication & Coordination

  • Notify plant personnel at field locations of upcoming and overdue preventive maintenance activities.

  • Coordinate equipment availability with plant managers and operations teams to support maintenance scheduling and service activities.

  • Serve as a primary contact between maintenance, operations, vendors, and technicians.

  • Communicate updates regarding maintenance schedules, equipment status, and repair progress.

Parts & Purchasing Support

  • Assist with identifying and ordering parts required for scheduled repairs.

  • Create purchase orders for parts, outside repairs, and vendor services.

  • Coordinate with vendors to support timely delivery of parts and services.

  • Track backordered or delayed parts and communicate potential impacts to maintenance schedules.

Documentation & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate maintenance records within the CMMS.

  • Ensure work orders contain complete labor, parts, and repair documentation.

  • Generate maintenance reports, service schedules, and supporting documentation as needed.

  • Monitor preventive maintenance compliance and equipment downtime metrics.

  • Support inventory control and parts management activities as needed.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve maintenance scheduling and workflow efficiency.

  • Assist with developing and maintaining standardized maintenance processes and procedures.

  • Support fleet reliability initiatives and preventive maintenance programs.

  • Reliable, regular attendance at the worksite or assigned work location.

  • Other duties and responsibilities related to the nature of the job may be assigned on a temporary or permanent basis as needed.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Experience

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience in fleet maintenance, equipment maintenance, service coordination, operations support or a related field preferred.

  • Experience using CMMS or similar fleet maintenance software preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Basic understanding of heavy-duty truck or construction equipment maintenance.

  • Strong organizational and multitasking skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

  • Excellent planning and scheduling abilities.

  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain accurate records and documentation.

  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.

  • Ability to prioritize competing tasks and adapt to changing operational needs.

  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across multiple departments.

  • Excellent communication and customer service abilities.

  • Must be able to effectively communicate and interact with both internal customers and external vendors.

  • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and Outlook.

  • Willingness to work a flexible schedule, including early mornings, nights, and weekends as required.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Lift objects of various dimensions and up to 30 lbs. of weight occasionally.

  • Ability to repeatedly climb stairs and ladders.

  • Ability to work in confined spaces.

  • Ability to repeatedly balance, bend from the trunk, crawl, kneel, push and pull objects.

  • Ability to repeatedly reach, squat, and tolerate prolonged standing, walking, and sitting.

  • Ability to work near, around, or on light or heavy equipment.

  • Ability to perform repetitive motions such as typing and data entry using a keyboard and mouse.

  • Ability to communicate clearly and effectively.

    • Onboard to Protege’s assessments and benchmarking business/ Take over ownership of the existing assessments pipeline and actively take on current relationships. Build a target account map of 15 to 20 vertical healthcare AI builders and begin identifying the path to our first contracts.

  • 60 days: Define strategy and drive active conversations

    • Run commercial conversations across accounts, driving towards active contracts. Define and propose the go-to-market strategy for the vertical.

    • Close first tranche of assessments customers

  • 90 days: Execute against strategic plan

    • Execute against the defined go-to-market strategy, continually sourcing new partnerships while driving forward the ones already in motion.

What You Bring:

  • Proven ability to run full-cycle commercial deals from first conversation through contracting in a complex business-to-business environment

  • Track record of building and executing an account strategy from scratch, including targeting, prioritization, and follow-through

  • Demonstrate skills navigating multi-stakeholder deals, including mapping technical and business buyers

  • Strong written and verbal communication with the ability to speak credibly to both technical and business stakeholders

  • Comfort operating with ambiguity and setting your own targets

  • Operational rigor in pipeline management, including accurate stage hygiene and clear reporting on strategy progress, what is working and what is not

  • Comfort in negotiating complex legal agreements

Working with Protege:

  • We move fast — thoughtfully.
    Speed matters in what we’re building, but so does intention. We’re biased toward action and always learning.

  • We’re a lean, high-trust team.
    Everyone has real ownership. Clarity and autonomy drive our best work.

  • We take our work seriously, not ourselves.
    We solve hard problems with humility and celebrate wins; big and small.

  • We’re kind, direct, and inclusive.
    We give feedback early and often, with the goal of helping one another grow.

  • We’re builders at heart.
    Every person at Protege is hands-on, resourceful, and focused on creating momentum.

  • We grow fast — together.
    You’ll be surrounded by people who care about impact, who challenge you to think bigger, and who are genuinely excited about what comes next.

title: Work From Home Client Service Representative | Entry Level
description:

Company: AO – American Income Division of Globe Life
Work Arrangement: 100% Remote | U.S. Residents Only
Schedule: Flexible | Work From Home
Experience: Entry-Level Welcome | No Prior Insurance Experience Required
Compensation: Commission-Based | Weekly Pay | Performance Incentives

Help Families Protect Their Future. Build Yours From Home.

Are you looking for a career where you can help families, build meaningful relationships, enjoy remote flexibility, and create long-term professional and financial growth through your performance?

AO is seeking motivated, service-oriented professionals to join our growing virtual team as Virtual Family Benefits Advisors.

In this role, you'll meet virtually with individuals and families seeking information about available benefits, help them understand their financial protection options, and provide personalized guidance based on their needs.

This opportunity combines customer service, benefits education, relationship management, and consultative insurance sales in a fully remote environment.

No previous insurance experience is required.

We provide comprehensive training, licensing guidance, mentorship, and ongoing professional development.

✓ 100% Work From Home
✓ Flexible Scheduling
✓ Qualified Client Opportunities Provided
✓ No Lead Purchasing Required
✓ No Traditional Cold Calling
✓ Weekly Commission-Based Pay
✓ Performance Bonuses & Renewal Income Opportunities
✓ Comprehensive Training & Mentorship
✓ Performance-Based Leadership Advancement

About AO | Globe Life

AO operates within the American Income Division of Globe Life, serving working families and members of organizations throughout the United States.

Our representatives help individuals and families understand supplemental life, accident, and health insurance benefits designed to provide additional financial protection.

We serve families connected with:

  • Labor unions

  • Credit unions

  • Associations

  • Working-family organizations

  • Veterans and their families

  • Other eligible groups and members

Our culture emphasizes service, integrity, accountability, mentorship, professional development, and performance-based growth.

What You'll Do

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Help Families Understand Their Benefits

As a Virtual Family Benefits Advisor, you'll conduct scheduled Zoom and phone consultations with prospective and existing clients.

You'll:

  • Learn about each family's needs and financial protection priorities

  • Answer questions regarding available benefits

  • Explain life, accident, and supplemental health insurance options

  • Review coverage features in clear, easy-to-understand language

  • Provide needs-based recommendations

  • Help families evaluate available options

  • Guide clients through applications and enrollment

  • Assist with required documentation

  • Maintain accurate digital client records

Our approach emphasizes education, service, integrity, and trust—not high-pressure sales tactics.

❤️ Build Long-Term Client Relationships

Your relationship with a family doesn't necessarily end after enrollment.

You'll provide continued service by:

  • Maintaining professional follow-up

  • Answering policy and benefit questions

  • Assisting with applicable policy reviews

  • Helping with beneficiary information updates when appropriate

  • Responding to ongoing service needs

  • Maintaining accurate client documentation

  • Building trust through dependable communication and exceptional service

The goal is to become a trusted resource families can rely on throughout their relationship with AO.

☎️ Qualified Client Opportunities – No Traditional Cold Calling

Representatives connect with individuals and families who have requested information regarding available benefits.

This allows you to focus on:

  • Scheduled virtual consultations

  • Benefits education

  • Needs-based conversations

  • Enrollment assistance

  • Relationship building

  • Follow-up

  • Ongoing client service

No lead purchasing is required.

Rather than spending your time searching for prospects, you can focus on serving clients and developing your professional skills.

🏡 100% Remote Work

Build your career from home while staying connected to clients, mentors, teammates, and leadership.

The virtual environment offers:

  • No daily commute

  • Virtual client appointments

  • Online training and coaching

  • Remote team collaboration

  • Modern digital business systems

  • Flexible scheduling opportunities

Remote flexibility also requires professionalism, accountability, organization, and consistent follow-through.

💰 Weekly Pay & Performance-Based Compensation

This is a commission-based independent contractor opportunity rather than an hourly or salaried position.

Compensation opportunities may include:

  • Weekly commission payments

  • Performance-based bonuses

  • Renewal and residual income opportunities

  • Leadership incentives

  • Recognition programs

  • Additional performance rewards

There is no predetermined cap on commission-based production; however, compensation is directly tied to individual activity, production, consistency, and results.

Individual earnings vary. No specific income level is guaranteed.

♾️ Renewal & Residual Income Opportunities

Building strong client relationships can create opportunities for long-term renewal income on eligible business.

As your client base develops, qualifying representatives may have opportunities to earn income associated with eligible policy renewals in addition to new production.

This rewards representatives who focus not only on enrollment but also on long-term client relationships and service.

📚 Comprehensive Training & One-on-One Mentorship

No Insurance Experience? That's Okay.

Candidates moving forward receive guidance and support through the licensing process.

📈 Career Growth & Leadership Development

At AO, professional growth is based on performance, consistency, initiative, and demonstrated leadership ability—not simply tenure.

Representatives interested in developing beyond an individual client-facing role may pursue opportunities in:

  • Training and mentorship

  • Team development

  • Coaching

  • Client relationship management

Potential development may progress from:

Family Benefits Advisor → Mentor/Trainer → Team Leader → Management → Advanced Leadership

❤️ Benefits & Professional Support

  • Recognition programs

Who We're Looking For

Ready to Build Your Future While Helping Families Protect Theirs?

If you're looking for a 100% remote career where you can help working families, build lasting relationships, develop professionally, and create long-term earning and advancement opportunities through your performance, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply today to be considered for our Virtual Family Benefits Advisor opportunity with AO – American Income Division of Globe Life.

Help Families. Build Relationships. Work From Home. Grow Your Future. 🚀

title: Safety Specialist
description:

  • Relocation Authorized: National - Family
  • Telework Type: Full-Time Office/Project

Extraordinary teams building inspiring projects:

Since 1898, we have helped customers complete more than 25,000 projects in 160 countries on all seven continents that have created jobs, grown economies, improved the resiliency of the world's infrastructure, increased access to energy, resources, and vital services, and made the world a safer, cleaner place.

Differentiated by the quality of our people and our relentless drive to deliver the most successful outcomes, we align our capabilities to our customers' objectives to create a lasting positive impact. We serve the Infrastructure; Nuclear, Security & Environmental; Energy; Mining & Metals, and the Manufacturing and Technology markets. Core to Bechtel is our Vision, Values and Commitments . They are what we believe, what customers can expect, and how we deliver. Learn more about our extraordinary teams building inspiring projects in our Impact Report .

Project Overview:

Bechtel is building a semiconductor manufacturing plant in New Albany, Ohio. We are partnering with the North America Building Trades Unions and suppliers to create several thousand new jobs and work with local education organizations to implement new training programs that will support the future talent pipeline. Bechtel Manufacturing & Technology, Inc. offers engineering, procurement, and construction services for customers in the semiconductor manufacturing, electric vehicle, and data center markets. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, the M&T global business unit also includes colleagues working in Arizona, Ohio, Texas, India, and additional project locations around the world.

Job Summary:

The Safety Specialist supports the implementation of project ESH programs by performing both administrative and field tasks in accordance with industry standards and regulatory requirements. This role applies to occupational safety practices to manage safety and health aspects of projects or facilities, with a primary focus on fieldwork. The position reports to an Area ESH Lead (or designee).

The job involves physical tasks such as walking around construction sites in very hot or cold weather conditions, climbing ladders and scaffolding, working at heights or on uneven ground, and accessing confined spaces. You must also be able to wear all required personal protective equipment (PPE), including items like harnesses, life vests, and gloves. #LI-AE2

Major Responsibilities:

  • Establish and maintain constructive working relationships with craft professionals, field supervisors, and subcontractor representatives.
  • Integrate safety and health requirements comprehensively throughout all project phases.
  • Provide technical expertise for risk assessments and conduct safety reviews to ensure regulatory compliance.
  • Research, interpret, and apply both organizational and regulatory standards, preparing accurate documentation and technical reports.
  • Contribute to the development and implementation of safety plans, permits, and training programs.
  • Participate in emergency response actions and incident investigations, including root cause analysis and corrective action tracking.
  • Communicate safety requirements clearly and facilitate their incorporation into project plans, contracts, and daily operations.
  • Conduct routine field inspections, monitor ESH performance, and verify adherence to all relevant standards.
  • Develop and disseminate ESH communications through presentations, bulletins, and digital platforms.
  • Collaborate with other ESH team members across all disciplines to provide comprehensive support as necessary.


Education and Experience Requirements:

  • Requires a Bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) related to occupational safety or health and 2-5 years of relevant experience or 6-9 years of relevant work experience


Required Knowledge and Skills:

  • Ability to research, interpret, and apply regulatory and organizational requirements (e.g., OSHA, ISO 45001).
  • Strong oral and written communication skills, including technical writing and report preparation.
  • Analytical skills related to sampling, monitoring, and recordkeeping.
  • Ability to conduct field inspections, program audits, and manage corrective actions through completion.
  • Proficiency with computers to develop reports or presentations, manage data and reports.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in utilizing digital safety management software to oversee ESH processes.
  • Adaptable and able to work outdoors in a field environment under various weather conditions.
  • Ability to support multiple work shifts, as needed, and a wide range of field related tasks.
  • Valid driver's license.

Additional Qualifications:
  • Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish is preferred but not required.
  • Experience in developing or delivering safety training or presenting to diverse audiences.
  • Ability to work in multicultural, multidisciplinary environments.
  • Knowledge and experience with ISO 45001 Management System and OSHA standards.
  • Professional certification (e.g., ASP, OHST, CSP, CIH) or progress toward certification is highly desirable.
  • Broad technical knowledge, science skills, and technical writing abilities.


Total Rewards/Benefits:

For decades, Bechtel has worked to inspire the next generation of employees and beyond! Because our teams face some of the world's toughest challenges, we offer robust benefits to ensure our people thrive. Whether it is advancing careers, delivering programs to enhance our culture, or providing time to recharge, Bechtel has the benefits to build a legacy of sustainable growth. Learn more at Bechtel Total Rewards

Diverse teams build the extraordinary:

As a global company, Bechtel has long been home to a vibrant multitude of nationalities, cultures, ethnicities, and life experiences. This diversity has made us a more trusted partner, more effective problem solvers and innovators, and a more attractive destination for leading talent.

We are committed to being a company where every colleague feels that they belong-where colleagues feel part of "One Team," respected and rewarded for what they bring, supported in pursuing their goals, invested in our values and purpose, and treated equitably. Click here to learn more about the people who power our legacy.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, age, national origin, disability, citizenship status (except as authorized by law), protected veteran status, genetic information, and any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. title: Senior AI Engineer
description:
Introduction

Since 1973, East West Bank has served as a pathway to success. With over 110 locations across the U.S. and Asia, we are the premier financial bridge between the East and West. Our teams of experienced, multi-cultural professionals help guide businesses and community members on both sides of the Pacific looking to explore new markets and create new opportunities, and our sustained growth and expertise in industries like real estate, entertainment and media, private equity and venture capital, and high-tech help build sustainable businesses and expand our associates’ potential for career advancement.

Headquartered in California, East West Bank (Nasdaq: EWBC) is a top-performing commercial bank with a strong foundation, an enterprising spirit and a commitment to absolute integrity. East West Bank gives people the confidence to reach further.

Overview

East West Bank is seeking an experienced Senior AI Engineering to design, build, and operationalize enterprise-grade AI and Generative AI solutions across the Bank. This senior technical leader will translate emerging AI capabilities into secure, scalable, production-ready banking applications that improve operational efficiency, risk management, customer experience, and employee productivity.

The role is expected to be hands-on at the outset while helping establish foundational AI engineering capabilities, operating standards, and a small, high-performing AI engineering team.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and deploy enterprise AI and Generative AI applications for prioritized banking use cases (e.g., customer service, fraud detection, document processing, knowledge management, and operational efficiency)
  • Architect LLM-enabled solutions spanning retrieval-augmented generation, vector search, agentic workflows, MCP, model orchestration, tool/function calling, and human-in-the-loop controls.
  • Build production-grade services and APIs using Python, FastAPI or Flask, Azure OpenAI, Azure ML, Databricks, ADLS, and modern cloud-native patterns.
  • Integrate AI capabilities into enterprise applications, developer workflows, knowledge management platforms, automation, analytics, and decision-support processes.
  • Establish engineering practices for CI/CD, testing, model evaluation, observability, performance optimization, security, and responsible AI controls.
  • Establish reusable AI engineering frameworks, reference architectures, code standards, deployment patterns, and governance controls to accelerate enterprise adoption.
  • Partner with business, data, cybersecurity, risk, compliance, legal, and vendor teams to ensure solutions meet regulatory, privacy, auditability, and operational risk expectations.
  • Prototype rapidly with stakeholders, convert pilots into scalable implementations, and define measurable adoption and impact metrics.
  • Evaluate LLM platforms for accuracy, latency, cost, security, explainability, and fit for regulated enterprise use cases.
  • Support hiring, mentoring, and day-to-day technical leadership of AI engineers and cross-functional delivery teams.
  • Stay current with emerging AI technologies and advise leadership on practical opportunities, risks, and implementation tradeoffs.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

AI Fluency & Hands-On LLM Skills

  • Hands-on experience with major LLM platforms, including OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot/Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, and open-source models such as Llama or Mistral.
  • Practical experience with prompt engineering, RAG, embeddings, vector databases, LLM orchestration frameworks, agentic workflows, evaluation frameworks, and hallucination mitigation.
  • Ability to design AI applications that include data protection, source validation, access control, logging, monitoring, traceability, and human review where appropriate.
  • Strong understanding of Responsible AI, model governance, prompt-injection risks, data privacy, and production controls for LLM-enabled solutions.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, AI/ML, or equivalent practical experience; advanced degree preferred.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in software engineering, AI engineering, platform engineering or related technology leadership roles, including experience delivering production AI solutions
  • Proven experience leading AI, data, automation, or emerging technology initiatives from strategy and experimentation through production delivery.
  • Strong hands-on engineering background in Python, API design, microservices, cloud architecture, distributed systems, data pipelines, CI/CD, testing, observability, and secure software delivery.
  • Deep experience with the Azure ecosystem, including Azure OpenAI, Azure ML, Databricks, ADLS, Azure AI Search, and related enterprise integration patterns.
  • Experience with LLM frameworks and tooling such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, vector databases, model registries, evaluation frameworks, and monitoring/observability tools.
  • Strong process and data discipline, including data quality, lineage, metadata, workflow design, controls, operational risk, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Experience in financial services, banking, fintech, insurance, or another regulated industry with strong understanding of compliance, auditability, risk management, and governance.
  • Ability to lead cross-functional teams, influence senior stakeholders, mentor engineers, and translate complex AI capabilities into practical business solutions.
  • Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to define AI roadmaps, operating models, standards, adoption plans, and success metrics.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in AI, Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field.
  • Experience establishing AI engineering teams, platforms, reusable delivery patterns, and enterprise AI standards.
  • Experience with copilots, enterprise search, intelligent document processing, workflow automation, and AI-enabled knowledge management.
  • Experience driving AI vendor evaluation and selection processes within regulated environments
  • Familiarity with model risk management, third-party/vendor risk, privacy impact assessments, and regulated technology delivery.
  • Experience with MLOps/LLMOps, AI monitoring, evaluation pipelines, model/prompt registries, and production incident management.
  • Track record of mentoring senior engineers and building high-performing technical teams.

Applicants must have legal authorization to work in the United States. We do not offer visa sponsorship at this time.

Compensation

The base pay range for this position is USD $175,000.00/Yr. - USD $275,000.00/Yr. Exact offers will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and location.

title: Upstream Technical Operations Intern

In addition, the role shall identify, develop and maintain credible relationships with healthcare professionals, providers and academic centres.

Bring energy, knowledge, innovation to carry out the following:

description:

The Advanced Practice Provider (APP) functions as a member of the Hand and Upper Extremity care team within Marshall Orthopaedics, providing comprehensive patient care in both clinic and surgical settings. Practicing primarily out of Marshall University Medical Center, the APP collaborates with supervising hand surgeons and interdisciplinary staff to deliver high-quality care across the continuum, including evaluation and treatment of hand, wrist, elbow, and upper extremity conditions.The role spans outpatient hand clinic, operating room first assisting, and post-operative follow-up.   • Strong ability to read and interpret blueprints, GD&T, and technical schematics.

  • Solid math skills and experience using precision measuring tools (calipers, micrometers).

Benefits

description:
Remote Customer Experience Specialist | Entry Level

You’ll connect with prospective candidates who have already applied or expressed interest in learning about one of our career opportunities, confirm their interest, schedule their next step, and follow up when needed.

Your role is straightforward but extremely important:

Connect → Confirm Interest → Book the Appointment → Follow Up → Help Candidates Show Up

You won’t be expected to conduct full interviews or explain every detail of the opportunity. Your primary responsibility is helping interested applicants successfully move through the scheduling process.

No previous recruiting or appointment-setting experience is required. Training and ongoing coaching are provided.

✓ Recruiting Experience
✓ Performance-Focused Environment
✓ Career Growth Opportunities

🎯 Your Main Goal: Get Interested Candidates Scheduled

As a Remote Phone Booker / Appointment Scheduler, you’ll help keep our recruiting pipeline active and organized.

  • Update applicant statuses

  • Maintain organized follow-up lists

  • Keep recruiting calendars current

  • Collaborate with recruiters and hiring managers

Your success helps turn applicant interest into completed interviews.

🔥 Warm Applicant Leads — No Random Cold Calling

You won’t spend your day calling random phone numbers trying to convince strangers to apply.

You’ll primarily connect with people who have already:

  • Submitted an application

  • Responded to a job advertisement

  • Expressed interest in a career opportunity

  • Started the recruiting process

  • Scheduled previously but need to reschedule

  • Requested additional information

  • Completed an earlier step and need assistance moving forward

That gives every conversation a clear reason from the beginning.

These are warm candidate follow-ups—not random consumer cold calls.

📲 What a Typical Call Looks Like

A typical conversation might be simple:

You contact an applicant who recently expressed interest, introduce yourself, confirm they’re still interested, and help them select an available time for the next step.

You may also:

  • Confirm the date and time of an appointment

  • Explain how the virtual appointment works

  • Help the candidate locate scheduling information

  • New applicants

  • Confirmed appointments

  • Missed appointments

  • Rescheduled candidates

  • Candidates requiring follow-up

  • Completed recruiting steps

Your follow-up can help reduce missed interviews and improve the overall candidate experience.

description:

Rewards for Results. We provide clear, competitive compensation designed to recognize measurable outcomes and real impact.

Define and communicate the strategy, desired outcomes, and investment priorities for our Risk customer value streams

Direct continuous discovery, Voice of the Customer, product analytics, and competitive research to identify important problems, strengthen differentiation, and anticipate market shifts
Frame complex choices and resolve portfolio tradeoffs using customer impact, business value, evidence, feasibility, and strategic fit

Establish measurable product outcomes; use customer, product, and financial evidence to inspect progress, learn, and adapt

Partner with Engineering and Design on scalable product practices, experimentation, AI-enabled experiences, and improvements to speed, quality, and learning

What you’ll bring:

8+ years of progressive product-management experience delivering enterprise software, platform, or SaaS products; governance, risk, and compliance experience is preferred
2+ years leading, coaching, and developing Product Managers or comparable product teams, including geographically distributed teams
Demonstrated success setting multi-product strategy, making investment tradeoffs, and achieving measurable customer and business outcomes
Deep capability in customer discovery, market and competitive analysis, product analytics, business cases, and go-to-market

  • Support plant asset performance assessments and Root Cause Analysis (RCA) efforts.

  • Support Management of Change (MOC) and plant compliance processes.

  • Assist with work management activities, including creation of notifications and purchase requisitions within SAP.

Technical Support

  • Perform data-based analysis using plant systems and software applications such as EtaPRO, PI, EDS, and other operational tools to support plant leadership decision-making.

  • Coordinate alignment meetings between Operations teams and support organizations, including Outage Planning, Maintenance, Environmental, Safety, Security, and Financial Planning & Analysis.

  • Facilitate work management processes through SAP work order, notification, and procurement activities.

  • Assist with monthly OPEX budget reviews and forecasting activities.

title: Videographer
description:
We are looking for a creative and experienced Videographer to join our team and be responsible for producing high-quality and engaging video content that reflects the company brand identity and supports its marketing objectives.

The Videographer will be responsible for the complete video production process, starting from planning and filming, through editing and post-production, to the final delivery of professional video content.

Responsibilities

  1. Shoot and produce high-quality videos for real estate properties, projects, and company activities.
  2. Handle video production using professional cameras and appropriate equipment, including lighting, audio equipment, gimbals, and other production tools.
  3. Produce professional property videos that effectively showcase properties, interiors, exteriors, features, and amenities.
  4. Create engaging short-form content for social media platforms such as Instagram Reels, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts.
  5. Edit and produce professional-quality videos from raw footage to final delivery.
  6. Add visual effects, text, subtitles, music, sound effects, logos, and other required elements.
  7. Perform color correction, color grading, and basic audio enhancement to ensure high-quality final output.
  8. Collaborate with the Marketing, Social Media, and Listing teams to produce the required content.
  9. Contribute to developing new video concepts and creative ideas for marketing campaigns.
  10. Stay up to date with the latest video production and social media content trends and apply relevant trends to company content.
  11. Organize and maintain raw footage, project files, and other video assets in a professional manner.
  12. Meet video production deadlines and complete requested revisions when required.
  13. Ensure all video content follows the company’s visual identity and quality standards.
  14. Cover company events, activities, campaigns, and other occasions when required.
  15. Properly manage, maintain, and organize video production equipment.

Requirements

  • Proven experience as a Videographer, Video Producer.
  • Strong portfolio demonstrating professional videography and video editing work.
  • Solid experience in professional video shooting and editing.
  • Strong knowledge of cameras, lenses, lighting, and audio equipment.
  • Proficiency in video editing software such as Adobe Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve.
  • Knowledge of Adobe After Effects and Photoshop is a plus.
  • Experience creating social media content, Reels, and short-form videos.
  • Experience in real estate videography and property walkthroughs is a strong advantage.
  • Good understanding of cinematography, lighting, framing, and composition.
  • Ability to transform marketing concepts into engaging visual content.
  • Ability to work independently and manage projects from filming through final delivery.
  • Ability to work under deadlines and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to high-quality work.
  • Willingness to travel to different locations for property shoots, projects, and company events when required.
  • Ability to stay updated with the latest video production and social media trends.

Job Description:

Job Title: Pay Station Clerk

About Hy-Vee

At Hy-Vee, we believe the shortest distance between two people is a smile. We're seeking people with a passion for customer service, a willingness to learn, and a commitment to being part of a team that strives to make our customers' lives easier, healthier and happier.

The Role and Why It's Important

Our Pay Station Clerks keep the dining and checkout experience running smoothly for customers enjoying everything our store has to offer. In this role, you'll operate the register, assist customers with their orders, and help maintain a clean and well-stocked environment so every visit is a great one.

If you enjoy working with people, take pride in doing things right, and thrive in a fast-paced setting, we'd love to have you on our team.

What You'll Do

No two shifts are exactly the same, but here's what you can expect:

  • Provide prompt, friendly customer service by greeting customers with a smile, learning their names, and making every interaction a positive one

  • Operate the cash register accurately, scanning product and processing all payment types including cash, checks, credit card transactions, in-store charges, coupons, and discounts

  • Answer the telephone promptly and provide friendly, helpful service to customers who call

  • Work with co-workers as a team to ensure customer satisfaction and a pleasant work environment

  • Assist in other areas of the store as needed and take on special projects as assigned

  • Maintain strict adherence to personal hygiene, dress standards, and all Hy-Vee policies and store guidelines

  • Report to work when scheduled and on time

Your Skills

To be successful, you'll need to be able to:

  • Follow detailed written or verbal instructions and work through tasks with a few concrete variables

  • Perform arithmetic calculations involving fractions, decimals, and percentages and make change accurately

  • Understand and follow verbal or demonstrated directions and communicate supply needs orally or in writing

Accountable and Reports to: Store Director; Store Manager; Assistant Managers of HWH, Perishables, Store Operations, and eCommerce; Service Managers

Physical Requirements

  • Frequently stand and walk throughout a shift in sales, food service, or delivery areas

  • Where applicable to the role: ability to safely use sharp knives and blades for food preparation

  • Where applicable to the role: exposure to heat- and burn-related hazards associated with cooking, baking, or grilling equipment

  • Where applicable to the role: ability to operate a delivery vehicle in accordance with applicable DOT standards

  • Perform repetitive standing, walking, reaching, and bending associated with order fulfillment, POS transactions, and cleaning/sanitation duties

​

Working Environment

This is a fast-paced role in a retail store and dining environment where you will be on your feet throughout your shift. You will have frequent exposure to temperature extremes and dampness, with possible equipment movement hazards and exposure to cleaning chemicals or solvents. Safety is always a priority, and training is provided to help ensure a safe and supportive work environment.

The anticipated hourly starting wage for this position is $13.00 to $16.25 depending on experience.

Your boots crunch through snow as you head over to greet your lesson. After introductions are made, a few moments are spent getting to know your class. It’s a perfect day for teaching. title: Cafe crew
description:
Looking for a Café All-Rounder

Who We Are

We are an artisanal beverage and modern toast cafe focused on quality and consistency. Our customers order via a self-service kiosk or QR, and our team focuses purely on crafting exceptional food and drinks, friendly communication, and maintaining an impeccable space.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a proactive, eager-to-learn individual to become the master of our workflow. No prior café experience is necessary. We will train you in our recipes and SOP. The single most important requirement is a great attitude!

title: UX/UI Design Co-op (Hybrid) - January 2027
description:
Term: January 2027

Duration: 4 or 8 months

Openings: 2 positions

Salary Range: $3,650- $4,525 CAD per month

Application Deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026, at 9:30 AM PDT

Your Opportunity

By joining the Kardium team, you can help make a difference in the lives of millions around the world. We have developed a ground-breaking medical device for the diagnosis and treatment of the most common heart rhythm disorder, atrial fibrillation – which can cause stroke, heart failure, and other heart-related complications.
Kardium’s mission is to deliver the best treatment for atrial fibrillation. To achieve this, we have developed The Globe® Pulsed Field System – we have a fantastic technical team that has developed a product with strong, unique, and customer-valued differentiators versus other solutions on the market. We have built connections with key opinion leaders who are already using the Globe System and are helping to tell our story.
We have obtained FDA and Health Canada approval and officially begun the commercial launch of the Globe® Pulsed Field System. This is a pivotal and exciting time in our journey, as we bring this life-changing technology to patients!
As a member of the UX/UI team, you will work closely with Product Management, Usability, and Software Development teams to update and promote our design system and design new interactions/UX improvements for the software that drives user interaction with the Globe system.
You will conduct heuristic/UX expert review of existing interactions and propose (and test) alternative designs, representing improvements to our software. Your work will help embed UX/UI best practices and adherence to regulatory guidelines.
You will be instrumental to ensuring best UX/UI practices for consistency, accessibility, and usability in software used in a highly technical domain.
Please note, this opportunity is a hybrid work arrangement, located in Burnaby, BC.
What You Will Experience
You will engage in activities that develop practical and transferable skills such as:

Support quick design tasks as well as longer-running design projects.
Research and promote inspirational UX/UI design patterns, including competitive analysis and benchmarks from other domains.
Create appropriately detailed design documentation to support the design process (wireframes, mock-ups).
Design detailed UX/UI prototypes and mock-ups to test with users and guide software development.
Communicate design guidance to product development teams.
Participate in hands-on user feedback sessions.
Design graphical elements and icons as part of the user experience.
Lead design activities as well as contribute to other designers’ work.
Occasionally provide design support to other teams in the company.

What You Bring to the Team
Our Kardium team is smart, creative, and passionate about creating cutting-edge medical devices to help improve people’s lives. We work within a collaborative environment based on trust and respect. And we understand that only by working together can we solve the unsolvable.
You will be successful in this role because you possess these attributes:

Partial completion of a degree or diploma in: UX design, interaction design, human computer interaction, digital media design.
Demonstrated experience creating UX /UI documentation, such as mock-ups, wireframes, and/or prototypes.
Experience with standard design tools: Figma, Adobe Suite (PhotoShop; Illustrator)
Demonstrated experience creating and working with components
Special interest in UI design: micro-interactions, color and visual design
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Exposure to UX/UI best practices from games, consumer applications, B2B applications regarding accessibility, visual design and interaction patterns.

Why Work at Kardium?
A meaningful Co-op/Intern term experience, working with truly innovative technology and an ambitious team, combined with:

Meaningful Work: Gain hands on experience working on projects that make an impact, giving you valuable experience to kickstart your career.
Community of Co-ops: Join a network of 40+ students across the company, with regular social events and monthly co-op events to connect with peers.
Development & Growth: Collaborate with engaged leaders and multi-disciplinary teams who are committed to supporting your development and growth.

Life at Kardium
What makes us a great place to work?

Our Purpose
Our People
Our Culture

At Kardium, we embrace diversity of background, experience, and perspective and we’re committed to inclusion and equity at every level. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates who represent the full diversity of all communities.
We collaborate with Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), as volunteer-led groups who share a common dimension of diversity and come together to provide support, education, and other opportunities across Kardium. Examples of our ERGs include Women ERG, Pride ERG, Race Ethnicity & Cultural Heritage (REACH) ERG, Truth & Reconciliation ERG, Persian Community ERG, Chinese ERG, Barangay Kardium (Filipino) ERG, Brazilian ERG and Irish ERG.
As part of your application, we encourage you to note if you require an accommodation for the recruitment process (including alternate formats of materials, accessible meeting rooms or other accommodations). There will be an optional section in the application form where you can provide this information to the recruitment team.
And our employees think we are great too – check out Glassdoor to learn more!
Compensation
Compensation for this role is based on multiple factors including your current year of study, the number of previous co-op terms completed, as well as market data.
Candidates must be legally entitled to work in Canada.
Relocation Support

Relocation Allowance: We offer a relocation allowance to support out-of-province students moving to Burnaby BC for their Co-op/Intern term.
Community Before Day One: Out-of-province students make up about 30% of each cohort. We connect all incoming students through email before the term starts to help with planning the move.
Questions? We're Here to Help: Relocating for the first time comes with a lot of questions. Our Talent team is happy to help with any questions that may come up.

How to Apply
To apply for this position, please upload three separate documents in PDF format via our Careers Page:

Cover letter
Resume
Most recent transcripts (to be combined in one PDF document, unofficial or co-op transcripts are acceptable)

Please note, there are also required questions to be completed, as a part of your overall application.

title: Sr. Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer

Ready to take your career global?

Make your mark at one of the biggest names in payments. We’re looking for a Sr. Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer to join our ever evolving IT Infrastructure team and help shape the future of global commerce.

The primary responsibility of this role is to design, optimize, support and further automate the cloud infrastructure supporting our business platforms, and to continuously improve the platforms to meet the evolving needs of Global Payments.

What you’ll own:

  • Formulate and carry-out business impacting cloud infrastructure-related designs, primarily in AWS and Azure, to meet the strategic direction and standards of the company and the cloud team, including ancillary services and on-premises services and hybrid solutions.

  • Support automated methodologies for build activities, such as for resource provisioning, hardening, leveraging PaaS offerings, load balancer rules and firewall policies.

  • Partake in ownership of engineering efforts, including new solutions design and optimization, for multiple engineering projects, concurrently, working closely with the business owners, product teams and applications teams.

  • Drive compliance and security efforts related to systems managed by the team

  • Support and continuously improve upon methods to improve stability and availability of infrastructure services

  • Work with the Project Managers and Infrastructure Coordinators on project progress, issues and solutions

What you’ll bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or similar field, or equivalent work experience.

  • Design and operations experience in both AWS and Azure environments.

  • 5-7 years of systems administration, design, engineering or commensurate IT technical experience.

  • Experience with enterprise repositories, namely GitHub Enterprise, as well as deployment management and CI/CD pipelines, namely through Jenkins and Harness.
  • Experience with multiple active scripting languages and strong IaC, including and especially Terraform, Ansible, PowerShell and Python.
  • Strong knowledge of multiple flavors of Linux and Windows Server, along with the experience in administering these systems through scripted/automated processes.

  • Understanding of the workings and operation of virtual environments, including VMware ESXi, vCenter, vCAC, VDIs, etc.)
  • Working knowledge of implementing automation orchestration across all life cycle environments

It’s a bonus if you have:

  • Experience with network principles and architecture

  • Experience with enterprise monitoring solutions

  • Experience with storage technologies and principles and SANs (e.g. Pure, Netapp, EMC)

  • Excellent communication skills are a must, such as to lead design discussions, planning sessions and triage.

  • A track record and understanding of what it means for full ownership of task, project and responsibilities

  • Ability to work independently, as well as part of a team.

  • Analytical and problem-solving skills; ability to demonstrate a proven troubleshooting methodology

  • Willing to work off-hours, including as part of an on-call schedule and during project release windows

  • Willingness to provide innovative ideas and solutions, even when they may initially seem unpopular

  • Possess and demonstrate good organization skills, task and time management skills, while understanding the importance of good work/life balance

About the team

Our inclusive and global teams win together every day. We’re proud to have the best minds in the industry, who you can learn from as you grow your career. The people, the energy, the connections – it’s unmatched. Come and be part of an ever-evolving company and get dynamic opportunities that go beyond borders.

What makes a Globalpayer?

Globalpayers think like a client, act like an owner and win as one team. We’re curious and innovative – always finding better ways to deliver impact. We empower each other to make decisions, and it’s our passion that drives excellence in everything we set out to do.

Does this sound like you? Then you sound like a Globalpayer. Apply now to take your career global.

Our perks - what we’ll bring for you

We know it’s bigger than just your career. It’s your life, and your world. That’s why we offer global benefits and programs to support you at every stage. Here’s a taste of what you can expect.

A competitive salary and benefits package that recognizes your contribution

Opportunities to grow your skills and build your career within a global business

Access to learning, development and on-the-job experiences that expand your expertise

A supportive, inclusive team environment where your ideas and input matter

Time to give back through community and charity initiatives

Recognition through a global platform that celebrates your achievements

title: Behavior Coach Outpatient Tempe
description:
GENERAL SUMMARY: The Behavior Coach role will provide intensive direct support services to families who have children that are “at-risk” by constructing programming that is unique to each client. A Behavior Coach will provide family, school-based interventions, and community centered interventions, which are guided by positive behavior support principles that address the needs identified by the CFT, the family, and the school. The Behavior Coach is responsible for meeting their clients where they are in the home, school and community, helping to support individuals in developing positive behavioral strategies to improve their social, emotional, and/or academic success. This role involves working with children and adolescents and their families and CFT teams to create and implement individualized behavior intervention plans and promote a supportive learning environment. Manage client caseload, review individualized service plans and maintain chart compliance for all clients.
JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

Develop and implement individualized behavior intervention plans, education and interventions for assigned children and families, based on assessments, data analysis and goals created in the Child and Family Team.
Provide assistance to children and families by identifying strengths and needs, accessing support, and collaborating with other departments and also partnering with other professional agencies.
Provide a minimum of 30 hours of face-to-face direct support services to enrolled clients.
Driving is required in order to be assessable to meet clients where they are in the community and adhere to clients availability hours.
Manage client caseload review service plans and out of compliance clients.
Assist and support the family in developing social and natural support networks by utilizing community resources.
Introduce parents to alternative parenting techniques (positive behavioral support).
Provide feedback to the Child and family Teams on progress and the interventions being utilized, or on barriers impeding progress.
Provide transportation to children and family as determined by the family’s Child and Family Team and service plan.
Provide crisis intervention and stabilization support as needed.
Attend scheduled department and agency meetings.
Attend all agencies required training and 1:1 coaching supervision, as assigned by supervisor.
Adhere to the agency’s approved administrative time requirements.
14.Assist in actively assessing work area for non-compliance issues and notify supervisor in a timely manner to ensure follow up.
Complete all required documentation and billing requirements accurately and in the assigned time frames.
Provide feedback to the Child and Family Teams and education providers on progress and the interventions being utilized, or on barriers impeding progress.
Provide weekly updates and new interventions regarding client status to guardians.
Complete monthly reports and distribute them to the CFT team.
Provide direct coaching and support to students to improve behavioral skills, emotional regulation, and coping strategies.
Conduct observations and assessments to identify behavioral challenges and track progress over time.
Support the implementation of positive behavior reinforcement programs within educational settings.
Serve as a liaison between schools, families, and external support services to ensure coordinated care.
All other duties as assigned by supervisor.

QUALIFICATIONS:

High school diploma or GED with 4 years of experience working with children with a mental health diagnosis,
Associate’s degree with 2 years of experience working with children with a mental health diagnosis,
Bachelor’s degree in behavioral health related field (i.e., Psychology, family studies, human development, sociology, etc.)
Previous experience as a behavior coach (preferred).
Bi-Lingual in Spanish (preferred).

REGULATORY:

Minimum 21 years of age.
DPS Level I fingerprint clearance (must possess upon hire and maintain throughout employment).
CPR, First Aid, AED certification, if required (must possess upon hire and maintain throughout employment).
Current, valid Arizona Driver’s License and 39-month Motor Vehicle Report and proof of vehicle registration liability insurance to meet insurance requirements, if required.
Initial current negative TB test result, if required (Employer provides).
